During New Light's mission to transport the Curtana Original, Lancis was tasked with carrying the sword itself in her Skíðblaðnir and remain 30km outside the combat area as a relay point.

When relaxing, Lancis has a tendency to nap on Floris. She reacts strongly to Lessar's outrageous suggestions, threatening violence if Lessar says one more word. After the British Halloween, Lancis searched for the Curtana Original's location using New Light's spiritual items.

Bayloupe is the leader of the magic cabal New Light, being the eldest at around 18 years old. She has long silver hair and wears the standard New Light uniform without a jacket. Her spiritual item is the Gjallarhorn, a pair of horns worn like headphones that gives her Steel Glove the power of thunder.

As the leader and big sister figure, Bayloupe tries to keep the others in line, especially Lessar. She does not tolerate Lessar's mischief during missions. Bayloupe is highly patriotic and willing to make enemies for the sake of the U.K., but will also admit fault if necessary for the country's sake.

Despite her young age, Bayloupe is a capable magician and fighter, able to pressure a member of the Amakusa Church before being caught in one of their traps. She can use magic to remotely contact the rest of New Light and a magic circle to unleash a barrage of green lightning.

Floris is a 15-year-old member of the magic cabal New Light. She has blonde hair and wears a customized New Light uniform with a jacket over her shirt and spats under her skirt. Her spiritual item manifests as a pair of small dragon wings on her back that can slow falls and recover allies.

Despite her age, Floris is mature and has leader-like qualities, giving orders to the rest of the team. Like the other members, she is very patriotic and willing to fight for the U.K. However, Floris is not as reckless as Lessar and values her life in the face of failure.

Floris can drive a car and is one of the more level-headed members of the cabal. She gained a grudge against Kamijou Touma after he freed her restraints in a crude manner, alerting her captors. Floris used her wings in an attempt to offset their fall after Touma jumped from a train with her.

Lessar is a member of the magic cabal New Light. She has long black hair with blond bangs and blue eyes, wearing the group's uniform with a dragon tail-like spiritual item. As a middle schooler, she is younger than Kamijou Touma.

Lessar is a loud, energetic girl prone to inappropriate remarks and shameless flirting, especially towards Touma whom she aggressively tries to seduce into joining New Light. Her impulsiveness sometimes causes trouble for her team. However, Lessar is still a capable and loyal magician, said to be New Light's strongest fighter.

Like the other members, Lessar wields a Steel Glove spear and is highly acrobatic thanks to her tail. She can use magic to create an explosive gust of wind and a communication spell through a animated pumpkin. Lessar later assists Touma during World War III and comes to Academy City to warn him about the magic god Othinus.

Isabella Theism is a gaunt silver-haired and brown-skinned female necromancer and member of Necessarius. She wears tattered rags, the clothes of the dead, along with a cracked heart necklace and skull symbol on her head.

Excitable and enthusiastic about death and the dead to the point of a bewitching smile, Isabella greatly enjoys her necromantic work and the thought of gaining new research material. She interrogates in disturbing ways but doesn't hold grudges. Isabella wears the clothes of the dead to become one with them and hear their words.

As a necromancer, Isabella specializes in crafting fake human corpses of high quality by rearranging pig and cow remains to match human anatomy and treating them with chemicals. These corpses can be remote controlled to inspire fear and confusion. She also performs divination through invoking the dead and uses Voodoo techniques.

Cutia Virginroad is a female member of Necessarius. She has a reputation alongside Ange Catacombs for skills that prevent them from being deployed to other countries.

Cutia has a carefree personality, speaking in a drawn-out lazy manner most of the time, but will show her true self if the situation calls for it. She and Ange protected the British Royal Family during their journey to Scotland when facing the reproduced Golden Dawn.

As a magician, Cutia uses combinations of noble blood and execution tools like her saw Alps. It acts as a red rusty saw on a leash, being a collection of sword rust holding the grudges of executed royalty and privileged. It automatically protects her and she can use it in spells by swinging it.

Ange Catacombs is a blonde and muscular female maid and member of Necessarius. She and Cutia Virginroad have a negative reputation preventing overseas deployment.

At an age desiring to meet normal people outside the magic world, Ange is overprotective of her autonomous suitcases or "coffins". She and Cutia were assigned to protect the British Royal Family on their journey to Scotland.

Ange has strong arms and uses her suitcases as tools, making them move on command for things like acting as footholds or capturing targets inside them. When saving Cutia from falling, she quickly arranged the suitcases as platforms and had one swallow an enemy beast.

Nics Everblind is a young male Necessarius magician lacking piety and purity, with the scent of one who makes a living through killing. He wears a baggy habit with a dragging hem and has one eye, the other socket used for prostheses.

Specializing in magic symbols represented through the body, Nics uses a large collection of prosthetic limbs and organs to modify and increase his capabilities beyond human limits. One prosthetic eye is the Shiva Imitation, based on the eye of Shiva, which can apocalyptically see the evil of the world.

During the Crowley's Hazards invasion, Nics selected the Shiva Imitation from Westminster Abbey before heading out with Ange and Cutia to protect the British Royal Family. He was the first defeated by the reproduced Golden Dawn.

Torquay Shadowmint is a male magician and member of Necessarius. He typically positions himself on church bell towers when on missions.

Torquay's magic involves using church bells which have inscriptions on them. By ringing specific bells in certain combinations and orders, he can produce effects described by linking the inscriptions to target any corner of the city the bells are located in. He uses a brass staff with several small bells on the end to remotely ring the larger bells.

During a mission when the Amakusa were being impersonated, Torquay attempted to bomb a tanker truck he believed them to be using from his position in a bell tower. However, noticing they had chosen a route passing by hospitals and student dormitories, he angrily called off his attack to avoid endangering innocent lives.

Freadia Strikers is a blonde-haired female magician of Necessarius. She wears a red outfit halfway between a dress and a suit. As the supervisor of the Amakusa Christians' admission test, she is stubborn, ruthless and suspicious, even using dangerous artifacts.

Freadia specializes in magic based on folklore legends of cursed jewels, using her crystal radio to transmit curses, and carries various jewel appraiser tools. During the test, she relentlessly pursued the Amakusa, convinced of their guilt in a frameup, and fought Itsuwa using the Sickle of Saturn prototype armor to push her magic to the limit. 

However, Freadia quickly forgave the Amakusa once their innocence was proven, even while recovering from severe injuries from her own magic backfiring. Her parents were imprisoned by the Anglicans for trying to leave the magic side, but she doesn't hate the Church for it.

Tsuchimikado Touzu, born Ashiya Touzu, is a man from Necessarius. He was forced to change his family name to pose as a relative of Tsuchimikado Motoharu, alongside Urabe Bishu, a task he greatly disliked. 

The Tsuchimikado family follows a naming scheme related to the seasons, with Touzu's first name (冬頭) containing the character for winter (冬). His original surname Ashiya is derived from the famous Onmyouji Ashiya Dōman, a rival of Abe no Seimei, who was Motoharu's ancestor.

Tsuchimikado Bishu, born Urabe Bishu, is a woman from Necessarius. Like Tsuchimikado Touzu, she was made to change her name to act as a relative of Tsuchimikado Motoharu, something she was not pleased about. Bishu suggested that Motoharu adopt an outsider girl as his sister to fool Academy City.  

Her original surname Urabe comes from a clan of diviners that used turtle shells at the Heian court. The Tsuchimikado family follows a seasonal naming pattern, with Bishu's first name (美秋) having the character for autumn (秋). She believes that despite Motoharu's doubts, three days is enough time to change the world.

Ureapaddy Exica is a swarthy Indian magician with grey/silver twin-tail hair, blue eyes and a bindi. She typically wears an orange belly dancer-style outfit with detachable sleeves, harem pants, a red loincloth, jewelry and high-heeled sandals. When in public, she dons a long orange sari over a yellow choli and skirt.

Ureapaddy is absolutely merciless to enemies and obstacles, even destroying her own cabal members with a smile for her destructive goals. However, this ruthlessness stems from a desire to protect her sister Sozty from sharing her cruel fate in magical experiments. Ureapaddy struggles with the contradiction between her methods and motives.

Through the Astra Reorganization combining her with others' spirits, Ureapaddy wields the powerful bow Brahma Astra, with arrows that bypass obstacles to annihilate 50m radiuses and can be amplified over 500,000 times to world-ending might. She hides her multi-armed sign-dancing Nataraj/Pinaka combo and uses other Astras like the electric Trishula.

The Víðarr Shoes Woman is an unnamed rough-looking female Necessarius magician with brown hair who appears to be around the same age as Kanzaki Kaori. She wears a t-shirt, miniskirt and two backpacks held by their straps.

Described as a belligerent person, the woman is quick to default to eliminating targets and shows little regard for the lives of prisoners or wardens when carrying out her orders. She engages in high-speed magical battles on the surface of water.

Her magic is based on the shoes of Víðarr, the Norse god of vengeance, which are made from discarded scraps of leather. By spreading triangular leather pieces polished with high-quality wax and stamping on them, she can greatly enhance her physical strength and that of her surroundings. She also uses concealment and defensive spells.

Ellasone is a large man who wears a cheap hooded coat. Despite an initial savage impression, there is an odd delicateness to his fingertips. He mainly works in London's craftsman district, specializing in the creation of magical restraints for the city's magical prisoners.

Though a criminal himself, Ellasone is protective of the young girl Seachel, letting her frequently visit him. He enjoys how she sees him as a hero, but feels guilty about benefiting from the Anglican Church's twisted human trafficking. Driven by his care for Seachel and sense of justice, Ellasone eventually rebels in an attack on the Church.

As a master of restraining tools and techniques, Ellasone can create powerful seals and traps on par with cathedrals. He skillfully analyzes and reverses existing magical defenses. His Voodoo-based white charm magic allows him to forcibly alter weapons, bind foes and compel truth.

Theodosia Electra is a female Necessarius magician specializing in Norse mythology-based magic. She has damaged hair that is a mix of blonde and silver, appearing to be in her late 30s or early 40s. Theodosia wears a baggy white top and faded white jeans.

Frequently changing her main spell, Theodosia has been noted to either be very talented or just easily bored, though her magic always remains Norse-based. At one point she used spells themed after the Little Match Girl fairy tale before revealing she was actually using Skírnir's Staff, which defends by manipulating space, unleashing explosive fire walls, and generating intense headwinds.

Despite her orders, Theodosia once temporarily betrayed Necessarius to protect the innocent Patricia Birdway, fighting her pursuer Stiyl Magnus. After her defeat, Stiyl realized the mission was wrong and the two worked together to defend Patricia from the true threat.

Jane Elves is a young witch from the Anglican Church who operates under Stiyl Magnus alongside Mallybath Blackball and Marie Spearhead. She has long green hair and wears a revealing outfit consisting of a hooded top with cat ears that barely covers her chest, a small cape on her shoulders, a black thong, stockings, and a garter belt. Jane also sports the Cross of St. George.

Despite her age and appearance, Jane is serious about her missions. However, she does have a complex about her short stature and enjoys making fun of Stiyl by calling him teacher. Jane and her two friends are working to incorporate rune magic into their self-taught magical abilities.

Jane's magic revolves around using a fan to control wind. Though it has no direct offensive power on its own, she can turn objects into dangerous projectiles or create defensive walls of wind. Like her allies and teacher Stiyl, she can also set up people-clearing fields and television camera-like displays using rune cards.

The Jeans Shop Owner is an unnamed man who runs a small but successful jeans store in London. He is also an unofficial member of the magic organization Necessarius. The man often works with Kanzaki Kaori, a customer at his shop, serving as her mission support. 

As one would expect from his profession, the Jeans Shop Owner is a fanatic about denim jeans. He adamantly refuses to sell any jeans to Kanzaki due to her habit of damaging them, as he considers stone-washing and cutting jeans to be unforgivable. Alongside his denim obsession, the man is also a pervert who shamelessly ogles women and tricks them into wearing revealing outfits.

The Jeans Shop Owner is skilled at reading people to discern if they're lying and has an in-depth knowledge of magical items related to cloth. He can understand their composition and purpose in order to reverse-engineer them as needed.

Onmyoudou is a traditional Japanese esoteric cosmology and system of occultism, which incorporates aspects of Taoism, Buddhism, Shintoism, and Chinese philosophy. It evolved into its current form around the late 7th century. Under the control of the imperial government and later the Tsuchimikado family up until the 19th century, it was eventually prohibited as superstition. 

Onmyoudou focuses on finding balance within oneself and the world through practices like divination, astrology, exorcism, and the use of shikigami. Shikigami, similar to a witch's familiar, are invisible spiritual servants which can be bound into small crafted manikins. Onmyoudou also makes use of the five Chinese elements of fire, water, earth, metal, and wood, balancing their constructive and destructive cycles.

Practitioners of Onmyoudou are known as Onmyouji. The most famous historical Onmyouji was Abe no Seimei, who was said to have established Onmyoudou during the Heian period. In the present day, his descendant Tsuchimikado Motoharu continues the practice, using Onmyoudou talismans and Feng Shui principles in his magic.

The Croce di Pietro is a powerful magical artifact belonging to the Roman Catholic Church, considered one of their Ten Holy Artifacts. At 1,800 years old, it takes the form of a pure white marble cross, 1.5 meters long and 70 cm wide. Its design, with a sharp tip and cross-guard pommels, gives rise to the mistaken legend that it is actually the Stab Sword, a weapon said to be able to kill any Saint in a single blow.

The Croce di Pietro's true power is to forcibly subjugate a location and its inhabitants to the dominion of the Church. To activate it, it must be erected in a Belvedere observatory to gather starlight from a specific constellation on a certain date, using the stars' positions like a magic circle to take control of the target area with a range of up to 47,000 square km. Under its effects, events in the controlled region will always benefit the Church, regardless of what actually happens.

The cross is said to be named for St. Peter, having first been used on his grave to establish the Vatican. Due to the strict conditions, it can only be used once per year for a given location. When not in use, it is kept sealed in a windowless vault and protected by an elite guard to prevent any light from touching it.

Lidvia Lorenzetti is a radical member of the Roman Catholic Church known as Mardi Gras. She has pale blonde hair, blue eyes, and wears white robes with a hood and red cross on the chest. 

Lidvia is utterly devoted to her faith and spreading the Church's gospel, even to those normally rejected by them. She has gathered many problematic people like criminals under her leadership. While increasing the Church's influence, Lidvia's unorthodox methods have made her a thorn in the side of her superiors. She revels in overcoming great challenges for her faith.

During the Daihaseisai, Lidvia and Oriana Thomson were tasked with using the Croce di Pietro to bring Academy City under the Church's control. Lidvia set up the cross outside the city while Oriana acted as a decoy. She believes subjugating the city is necessary to counter the growing influence of the Science Side and bring the world back to God's path. Though the plan failed, Lidvia's conviction never wavered, even when offered a chance to renounce her loyalty to the Church to save her own life.

Mallybath Blackball is a young witch and subordinate of Stiyl Magnus in Necessarius. She has wavy brown shoulder-length hair and wears a witch hat with a ribbon, a loose black robe with white accents, and high-heeled shoes with ankle straps. 

Serious about her missions, Mallybath also has a naive and clumsy side, lacking experience in real combat situations which leads to her being rescued by Stiyl multiple times. She works together with her fellow witches Jane Elves and Marie Spearhead, deferring to Marie's leadership.

Mallybath uses magic derived from the element of earth, controlled through her feathered pen. By touching the ground, she can trap targets by causing rocks to jut out and ensnare them. Like her teammates, she can also hide within her element for an indefinite time. Mallybath is capable of creating pillars of earth, but her magic is most effective when combined with the abilities of Jane and Marie.

Marie Spearhead is a mature-looking witch who serves as the leader of the trio under Stiyl Magnus, which includes herself, Mallybath Blackball, and Jane Elves. She has long, wavy blonde hair that covers her left eye and wears a pointed witch's hat with a ribbon. Her dress shows some cleavage, and she carries a broom adorned with a cat charm. Like her companions, Marie wears the Cross of St. George, white evening gloves, and heeled shoes with straps.

While serious about her missions, Marie has a playful side, happily disguising herself as a waitress to sneak up on a target. She calls Stiyl "teacher" to tease him, having approached him to help incorporate rune magic into her and her friends' self-taught magical abilities.

Marie's magic revolves around water, controlled using her broom and its cat pendant. By chanting and making the pendant glow, she forms large pillars of water to assault enemies. She can also freeze water into small lances or pellets. Her magic is more powerful in tandem with Mallybath and Jane's abilities, and she can hide underwater indefinitely like Mallybath.

Sherry Cromwell is a magician from the Anglican Church, Necessarius. She has messy blonde hair like a lion's mane, brown skin, and wears tattered black gothic lolita clothing with frills. Her magic name is Intimus115. 

A troubled woman, Sherry is driven by the desire to avenge her deceased friend Ellis, but also wishes to prevent conflict between the Magic and Science Sides. She has a contradictory nature, with her actions stemming from not wanting to lose anyone else dear to her. While usually brusque, she hoped someone would stop her destructive rampage.

Sherry is a master of Kabbalah and golem magic, her most powerful being Golem Ellis. Using magic circles drawn with chalk, she can summon a golem from nearby materials, controlling it remotely. The golem can regenerate, incorporate objects to repair itself, or be detonated by Sherry. She can also create remote-controlled mud eyes for spying. As an interpreter, Sherry decodes grimoire codes in paintings through their pigments and themes.

Smartvery is a witch stationed on the Coven Compass mobile fortress belonging to the Anglican Church. She has short, light brown hair and wears a black witch hat and robe with white accents.

As a witch, Smartvery is capable of using potions derived from magical plants to grant the ability of flight to objects and her own body. She can attack using her flying broomstick. Additionally, Smartvery can utilize communication spells and has mentioned being able to use an ocean control spell.

While facing the Knights of England during their rebellion, Smartvery suggested luring them beyond the United Kingdom's borders where the knights' empowering Curtana Original would not function, either fleeing entirely or attacking with the Coven Compass' weaponry. She recognized the limitations of the knights' violent approach compared to the influence possessed by the Royal Family.

Slappar is a young man with pale skin and a sickly complexion. He is the manager of the magical facility known as Brick Wharf.

At some point, Slappar created a being called Alfar from a fossil in order to overcome a personal defect preventing him from casting complex spells. He kept Alfar isolated within restricted areas of Brick Wharf, communicating with her through thick glass. However, after Alfar saw a cat and wished to pet it, she left her designated zones and discovered the truth of her origins and effects on other lifeforms. As a result, Alfar drove out Slappar and took over the facility.

Slappar is capable of using rune magic and acid-based spells. By preparing a tanker of supercooled water, he can create millions of microscopic runes to empower his magic. He can melt walls with waves of acid and intended to use Alfar to evolve himself while disregarding the harm to the environment it would cause.

Brick Wharf is a magical facility located in northern Scotland, serving as the core of the northern British defense line against invaders. It covers an area of about 400 square meters, consisting of a harbor and many red brick buildings. The facility originated during the Industrial Revolution before later being remodeled by the Anglican Church.

Brick Wharf houses a long-range Interception Spell with a 200km range. The spell analyzes the magic used by hostile magicians and sends out the most effective counter-signal, causing the target's magic to go out of control through an invisible magical bombardment over 1 meter in diameter. It can lock onto 50 targets simultaneously and attack 20 of them instantly.

During the incident caused by its manager Slappar in his attempts to overcome his limitations and evolve using the artificial being Alfar, Kanzaki Kaori and a group from Necessarius were sent to Brick Wharf. Alfar had rebelled and taken over the facility to isolate herself and prevent further distortions to the environment. After a struggle, Slappar was defeated and taken away while a means to seal Alfar's ability was sought out.

The Bishop of St. Julian's Cathedral is an elderly, unnamed male character affiliated with the Anglican Church. He received his position as a reward for supplying a large number of personnel to Necessarius. However, the bishop had actually established a twisted human trafficking system where he would arrange for civilian children to lose their parents and be taken in as trainee magicians, serving as a potential source of replacements in case of heavy losses to the organization.

The bishop is utterly remorseless about the lives he has manipulated and the suffering he has caused to innocent children for his own advancement. During Ellasone's attack on St. Julian's Cathedral in response to the bishop's actions, the bishop was captured and interrogated by the magician using magic tools that would punish him for lying, and would likely have been killed if not for Kanzaki Kaori's intervention.

Rachel is a friendly young nun of the Anglican Church. Though her exact appearance varies between the novel and manga adaptations, she is consistently portrayed with a caring and affectionate personality, especially towards her old friend Index.

During the British Halloween, Rachel approached Index, pinching her cheek, offering her food, and reminiscing about how they used to play together. However, Rachel had forgotten about Index's memory erasure, confusing the young nun. Several other nuns quickly joined in, gushing over Index's cuteness and attempting to give her more food.

Rachel's history with Index implies she has been part of the Church for a long time. Her simple gestures of familiarity and kindness suggest a warmth that Index rarely experiences in her turbulent life.

Dion Fortune is the current Archbishop of the Anglican Church and a magic user based on the real historical figure. As a grimoire-based recreation, she appears as a short, skinny girl with red hair, wearing a frilly white and pink dress with star decorations, along with purple leggings and thick-soled shoes. She carries a black box spiritual item called the Archetype Processor.

Fortune has a haughty and prideful nature, referring to herself as "The Great Dion Fortune". She claims to use her randomized magic to rebuild old, inefficient traditions into newer, smarter spells. However, she has a crippling fear of her old teacher Mina Mathers due to past trauma. Fortune was saved and befriended by Hamazura Shiage, causing her to assist him using her magic.

Dion's magic is channeled through her Archetype Processor, which transforms spells and items put into it into unpredictable new forms. This lets her confuse enemies and counter their plans with sheer chaos. By using it on the remains of her fellow recreated Golden Dawn magicians, she stopped Coronzon from hijacking the UK's magic system in the final battle.

School District 18 is one of the larger districts in Academy City, known for its prestigious schools dedicated to ability development. The district contains top institutions like Nagatenjouki Academy and Kirigaoka Girls' Academy. District 18 utilizes a separate scholarship program from the rest of the city.

The district is structured logically but feels thin in terms of life and activity. Road widths are uniform and the architecture is designed to discourage straying from the rules. Judgment member Shirai Kuroko has described it as a prison for children but a paradise for adults.

During incidents threatening the city, defensive lines have been set up in District 18 to halt the advance of intruders. The district is also home to the Elementary Particle Engineering Laboratory, a domed stadium, and the Anti-Skill Chemical Analysis Center which handles the city's forensic investigations.

Nagatenjouki Academy is one of the five most prestigious schools in Academy City, supposedly the best. Unlike Tokiwadai Middle School, entry is not restricted to espers, with students without abilities also being admitted. It has beaten Tokiwadai in a previous year's Daihaseisai.

Despite its elite status, Nagatenjouki has struggled to produce Level 5s, with Jounan Asako, a former Power Development Supervisor, being removed from her position for failing to do so within her term. The school uses the season "winter" (冬) as a naming theme.

Notable students of Nagatenjouki include the expelled Nunotaba Shinobu and Aizono Mio. Accelerator is also affiliated with the school according to documents. Staff members include the counselor Saitou Souta and former supervisor Jounan Asako.

Kirigaoka Girls' Academy is an all-girls school located near the Elementary Particle Engineering Laboratory in School District 18. It contains facilities for middle school, high school, and college levels. 

As one of the more prestigious academies in the city, Kirigaoka is dedicated to raising students with rare abilities. A student's rank is measured by the rarity of their ability rather than its level, with a minimum Level 2 requirement for enrollment. The standard uniform consists of a dark blue blazer with the school emblem, red necktie, white dress shirt, and matching blue skirt.

Kirigaoka is a leading expert in unconventional esper theories and conducts various research, such as that related to the Imaginary Number District and Kazakiri Hyouka. However, it also has connections to the dark side of Academy City. Notable students include Himegami Aisa, Kazakiri Hyouka, Musujime Awaki, and Kouzaku Mitori.

The Daihaseisai is a major annual sporting event and one of the biggest festivals in Academy City. Taking place over seven days in September, it involves students from all schools competing in various athletic events while esper abilities are permitted. The event is broadcast worldwide and the city is open to outside visitors during the festival period.

The Daihaseisai serves to improve Academy City's public image and allows schools to evaluate their esper development programs. Students are divided into red and white teams, with matches contributing points to their school's overall score. Events range from track races to more combat-oriented contests. Security is heightened yet strained during the festival.

The Daihaseisai forms the backdrop for several major story arcs in the series. Plots such as Lidvia Lorenzetti's use of the Croce di Pietro have unfolded behind the scenes of the festival. Other activities include the Night Parade at sunset each day.

The Elementary Particle Engineering Laboratory is a reinforced concrete square building located near Kirigaoka Girls' Academy in School District 18. It was used to study elementary particles and housed a special manipulator for microscopic object interference called Tweezers.

During the Battle Royale Arc, the laboratory's security was disrupted by the assassination attempt on Oyafune Monaka. This created an opening for the dark side group School to infiltrate the facility and steal the Tweezers.

A battle subsequently broke out between School and the group Item, who had anticipated School's actions. The conflict resulted in heavy damage to the building and the death of the School member Yobou Banka at the hands of Mugino Shizuri.

The Tweezers, also known as the Pincet Glove, is a special attachment-type manipulator developed for microscopic object interference. It allows researchers to grab particles smaller than atoms by using magnetism, light waves, and electricity to "absorb" them. The device is normally kept in a larger form to prevent theft, appearing as a metal glove with long glass claws on the index and middle fingers. Inside the claws are thinner metal stakes used for measurements.

The Tweezers played a key role in the plans of the dark side group School. Kakine Teitoku stole the device from the Elementary Particle Engineering Laboratory in order to gain access to the mysterious UNDER_LINE network. After his defeat, Tsuchimikado Motoharu of the group known as GROUP recovered the Tweezers and used it to decode data, discovering the existence of DRAGON.

Yobou Banka, also known as the Boy with Goggles, was a Level 4 Psychokinesis esper and former operative of the dark side group School. He had somewhat spiky hair and wore a puffy vest over his shirt, but his most distinctive feature was the Saturn-like ring of metallic goggles encircling his head with numerous plugs and cables connecting to a machine on his back.

A former challenger to Kakine Teitoku for the position of Level 5, the bitter defeat and subsequent trauma led Yobou to join School. He had an easygoing personality and didn't hesitate to kill to silence liabilities like the School member Management. His esper ability allowed him to skim fragrance components, demonstrated when he copied the contents of an Indian Poker card onto a blank one.

Yobou infiltrated the dark side group Member as a middleman for School under the leadership of Kihara Gensei. He was later killed by Mugino Shizuri in a battle between School and Item at the Elementary Particle Engineering Laboratory while attempting to steal the Tweezers. Mugino took his blood-spattered goggles as a trophy.

Saitou Souta was a kind and hardworking man who worked as a counselor at Nagatenjouki Academy. He helped to restore the humanity of Aizono Mio, a student subjected to harsh training and conditioning in the White Alligator project. Saitou's efforts to track down and aid the other White Alligator girls demonstrated his caring nature.

Unfortunately, Saitou ended up in a coma due to overwork after continuously being pushed the unpleasant jobs that other faculty members refused. The accident was covered up by Nagatenjouki Academy. This event deeply affected Aizono Mio and led to her seeking revenge against those she considered responsible.

Nunotaba Shinobu is a child prodigy formerly affiliated with Nagatenjouki Academy and a key figure in the Sisters Arc. She supervised the Testament machines used in the Radio Noise Project and was the first person directly involved that Misaka Mikoto encountered. Shinobu has an aloof demeanor, unkempt hair, wide "fish eyes", and wears gothic lolita style clothing.

Originally viewing the Sisters as mere test subjects, Shinobu's perspective changed after interacting with them. Realizing their humanity, she rebelled against the project and attempted to install emotions into the clones to make the researchers reevaluate their treatment. Though her efforts failed, Shinobu's actions deeply impacted Mikoto.

Following her expulsion from Nagatenjouki, Shinobu was later coerced into working on the Chemicaloid Project by the group STUDY due to her early research being used as the basis for the Chemicaloids. She formed a close bond with the Chemicaloid Febrie and worked to give her and her "sister" Janie a better life, ultimately being rescued from her situation through Mikoto's actions.

Jounan Asako is a former Power Development Supervisor at Nagatenjouki Academy and later an Anti-Skill officer. She has purple eyes and brown hair styled with a part on her right that exposes her forehead. Asako wears the standard Anti-Skill uniform with a yellow jacket.

After failing to produce a Level 5 esper within her term at Nagatenjouki, Asako was relieved of her position. The setback caused her to develop a plan involving experimenting on espers' reactions to stimuli. Her scheme involved a device emitting electromagnetic waves at frequencies that caused unease in Electromasters, fueling the urban legend "Someone's Watching You."

Misaka Mikoto ultimately fell victim to the effects of Asako's device. However, the combined efforts of Mikoto, Shirai Kuroko, Uiharu Kazari and Saten Ruiko exposed her plans. Asako was apprehended while attempting to flee Academy City.

Isoshio is a female teacher at Kirigaoka Girls' Academy. She is known for having published a thesis on why cats cannot use esper abilities.

According to Isoshio's research, animals require a minimum intelligence level equivalent to that of a five-year-old human child to develop esper powers. As most animals have an intelligence closer to a two-year-old human, they are unable to gain such abilities.

Experiments based on Isoshio's thesis seemed to support her conclusions. However, some like Yomikawa Aiho remain skeptical, believing that researchers would struggle to even determine if an animal's ability had manifested in the first place.

Aizono Mio, also known by the nickname Shinigami Kakiko, is a Level 4 esper and student at Nagatenjouki Academy. She has green eyes and long brown hair worn with a fringe at the front. Mio's Nagatenjouki uniform consists primarily of blue and white, with a red tie, black shoes, socks, and red wrist and neck accessories.

Mio was subjected to harsh training as part of the White Alligator project, which aimed to mass-produce Level 4 espers. The experience left her mind unstable until she was aided by the school counselor Saitou Souta. After Saitou fell into a coma due to overwork, the incident being covered up by the school, Mio sought revenge against those she deemed responsible.

As a Level 4 esper, Mio possesses the ability Military Oil, which allows her to control and alter the properties of oil and petroleum-based products. She can form weapons like missiles and blades, generate an armor dress capable of withstanding railgun shots, and ignite the oil for propulsion or incendiary damage. Mio received anti-railgun training as part of the White Alligator project.

Kouzaku Mitori, nicknamed Mii-chan, is a Level 4 esper and former test subject of the Clone Dolly project. She has purple hair styled in twin tails and matching purple eyes. As a child, she wore her hair short. Kouzaku often dresses in punk and gothic fashion, such as skull accessories and a black blazer over a white shirt and skirt.

Kouzaku befriended the Clone Dolly prototype, Dolly, while in the research facility. Discovering the truth behind the cruel experiments performed on her friend, Kouzaku rebelled but failed to save Dolly. The incident drove her to seek revenge against the dark side of Academy City. She later served as a liaison for the group Member under the orders of Kihara Gensei.

With the esper ability Liquid Shadow, Kouzaku can control high density liquids, specializing in liquid metal. She commonly shapes the metal into a puppet resembling herself, which she can manipulate remotely and use to create weapons. Kouzaku can control a massive quantity of metal at once and threaten a large area. After her defeat by Shirai Kuroko, she began working as an informant for Shokuhou Misaki while caring for a clone of Dolly.

External Connection Terminals are special facilities in Academy City that allow connection to the internet outside the city's closed network. There are four terminals located in the north (District 3), south (District 2), east (District 12), and west (District 13) of the city. All external lines connecting to the outside must pass through one of these terminals.

In an emergency, all the External Connection Terminals can be cut off to completely isolate Academy City's network from the outside world. This feature was utilized during the Battle Royale Arc, when the dark side group Block hacked the terminals alongside the Virus Isolation Center in order to confuse the network security team while they took control of the Hikoboshi II satellite.

Block was an Academy City dark side organization originally tasked with monitoring the level of cooperation from institutions outside the city. Led by Saku Tatsuhiko, its known operatives included Teshio Megumi, Yamate, and Tetsumou. Block had a liaison who served as a middleman with the higher-ups and could command Powered Suits.

After the 0930 incident, believing they could challenge Aleister Crowley's control, Block rebelled and hired 5000 mercenaries in a plan to infiltrate the Reformatory, take hostages, and assassinate Aleister using a Synchronous Multilayer Bomb. Despite their preparations, the plan was foiled by GROUP. Block was decimated in the ensuring conflict, with Yamate killed and Tetsumou injured beforehand by the mole Etzali. Saku and Megumi were later defeated by GROUP after taking control of the Reformatory.

In the aftermath, the remnants of Block were reorganized with the remnants of the other dark side factions Item, School, and Member to form a new organization. This organization was later dissolved following World War III.

Saku Tatsuhiko was the leader of the dark side organization Block. Described as a large, serious "bear-like" man with a crew cut hairstyle, he had an extreme hatred for Aleister Crowley and led Block in a rebellion to assassinate him.

As Block's leader, Saku monitored institutions outside Academy City. After the 0930 incident, believing Aleister's control could be challenged, he seized full control of the organization from its liaison and hired 5000 mercenaries for Block's plan. Saku was cold to those who became a liability, like Tetsumou, and unforgiving to traitors like Yamate (unaware Etzali had killed and replaced him).

Saku and Megumi led the mercenaries in taking control of the Reformatory to take hostages, but were confronted by Tsuchimikado and Awaki. When Megumi argued against his continued use of bombs and hostages with Awaki present, an enraged Saku threatened to kill her, leading Megumi to knock him out. He was likely apprehended afterwards.

Security robots are automated cylindrical machines designed to protect security and enforce rules in Academy City. Costing 1.2 million yen per unit, they are mobile criminal surveillance devices commonly seen patrolling the city's streets.

The robots have a distinctive barrel-shaped metallic body, usually moving on rollers. They can stand on retractable legs to appear larger and intimidating. The machines possess a robotic voice used to alert people and report to superiors, accompanied by a siren.

Equipped with compartments that can open to reveal net launchers, security robots are employed by Anti-Skill in front formations and as barriers during firefights, implying significant durability. Besides patrolling and handling troublemakers, they can also store water for extinguishing small fires. The robots can navigate elevators and are programmed to repeat attempts at overcoming certain obstacles before temporarily giving up and going elsewhere.

Member was a dark side organization in Academy City that answered directly to Aleister Crowley. Its known operatives included Professor, Baba Yoshio, Xochitl, and Saraku. Like other such groups, it was an unofficial unit composed of a small number of individuals. Member carried out Academy City's dirty work under Aleister's orders, with the Board of Directors also having some degree of command over them.

Member had a female liaison who served as a middleman with the higher-ups. Kouzaku Mitori later took over this role for a time. The group also had a large support staff and subordinate organization of grunts for various tasks. During the Battle Royale Arc, Member's leader Professor was killed by Kakine Teitoku, Yoshio confined himself, and Xochitl defected, leaving the group in shambles.

The remnants of Member were later reorganized together with the remnants of the other dark side factions Item, School and Block to form a new organization following the incident. This organization was dissolved after World War III.

Teshio Megumi was a tall and muscular woman with short hair who acted as the right-hand operative to Saku Tatsuhiko in the dark side organization Block. She normally wore a gray suit with a short camouflage shirt or sports bra.

In contrast to Saku's ruthless nature, Megumi had a softer personality and argued against the use of excessive force. Her outlook stemmed from a past undercover mission in Anti-Skill that exposed her to the dark side's exploitation of Child Errors who couldn't even speak. Megumi sought the truth behind their treatment, suspecting Aleister Crowley's involvement.

An expert in hand-to-hand combat, Megumi easily overwhelmed Tsuchimikado Motoharu before facing Musujime Awaki. She knocked out Saku when he threatened to kill her for protesting his actions. Against Awaki, Megumi initially had the upper hand, but was eventually defeated by the Move Point user's determination, though the esper had secretly held back against her.

Yamate was a young male operative of the dark side organization Block. He had a lean build and parted his hair down the middle. Despite being one of Block's central members privy to their plans of rebellion against Aleister Crowley, he was not actually that strong.

During Block's efforts to cover up the plans of the group School by destroying evidence, Yamate led an armed team to assault the apartment of the School member Management in Family Side. However, he had the misfortune of encountering the magician Etzali there.

Etzali, who had disguised himself as Unabara Mitsuki, was forced to attack one of the Block members and take their appearance to escape. Yamate ended up as the unlucky victim. Etzali killed him, stuffed his corpse in a closet, and assumed his identity. Etzali was then stuck undercover as the supposedly important Yamate, indirectly monitoring Block's activities.

Tetsumou was a petite young female operative of the dark side organization Block. She had a gloomy demeanor that contrasted with the serious soldiers around her. Tetsumou wore a short pixie cut hairstyle and the sailor uniform of an unknown school.

Using her esper ability Skill Polygraph, which allowed her to verify a person's profile through skin contact, Tetsumou served as Block's lie detector to root out traitors. She used an inhuman mechanical voice when reading the information. Besides a person's identity, Tetsumou could even uncover important facts about their past.

When Etzali infiltrated Block disguised as the deceased Yamate, he spiked some hand cream with liquid explosives to avoid being exposed by Skill Polygraph. The cream was picked up by a minor grunt, whose hand burst into flames when Tetsumou touched it, the shock and blood loss rendering her unconscious. Saku had the grunt executed as the perceived traitor and left Tetsumou's body to his men, seeing her as useless now that she couldn't detect traitors.

The Voice on the Phone refers to the mysterious, unseen individuals who communicate with and give orders to the dark side organizations of Academy City, serving as a liaison between them and the higher-ups.

They provide information and issue penalties for disobedience, such as shutting down Accelerator's choker, and may command Powered Suits. The liaisons are held responsible by their superiors when an organization goes rogue. It's implied that they are involved with recruiting new members.

While it's unclear if it's always the same person or multiple individuals using disguised voices, they seem to be a fairly small group given their high responsiveness. Besides the key figures like the Group and Item liaisons, there are handlers for the other factions such as School and Member.

Academy City's Independence Day is a holiday event celebrated each year on October 9th, commemorating the city's recognition as an independent territory despite being located within Japan. 

During this holiday, security is more lax than usual due to officers being diverted to aid in war efforts abroad. Many different factions and individuals from the city's dark underbelly take advantage of this reduced security to carry out various agendas and schemes.

In the timeline of the story, the Independence Day occurring in the first year marks a major incident involving multiple factions clashing as they each attempt to pull off their own objectives amidst the lowered defenses of the holiday.

Toomine Kanari was a researcher and doctor who worked at Clone Dolly Ideal, the third laboratory of the Clone Dolly Workshop. She was the main caretaker for the mysterious girl nicknamed "Ghost" by Yuuri Senya. Toomine had brown hair tied up in a bun, with long fringes framing her face, and was often seen wearing a labcoat over her clothes. 

Having always dreamed of being a hero who could save children after watching tokusatsu shows in her youth, Toomine studied science and joined Clone Dolly Ideal after graduating from Oua University. While initially coming across as callous to the child test subjects there, Toomine was actually the only researcher who truly cared about them.

Alone with the Ghost Girl, Toomine acted in a motherly fashion, trying to provide whatever she wanted without the girl needing to ask, showing the deep bond between them. Sadly, by the present time of the story, Toomine had passed away at the age of 23.

The Professor, whose real name is unknown, was an elderly man who served as the leader of the dark side organization known as Member. Short in stature at 160 cm, he had a notable appearance with long hair that stood on end, rectangular glasses, and a labcoat worn over his shirt and tie.

As a high-ranking member of the dark side, the Professor was highly intelligent but ruthless. His loyalty and obedience to Aleister Crowley stemmed from a belief that Aleister could help him attain his ideal of finding beauty in the world, which had shifted to a love of efficient formulas after art had brought him despair in his youth.

The Professor commanded the Mimosa nanodevices, which he would use to attack and try to retrieve the Tweezers from Kakine Teitoku. However, the Mimosa were blown away in the confrontation, and with the Professor left defenseless, Kakine killed him.

School District 12 is the easternmost district of Academy City, known for its concentration of religious facilities, occult studies, and theology schools, all approached from a scientific perspective. However, rather than faith, the district focuses on analyzing the psychology behind why humans believe in the supernatural.

The district's architecture is a mix of reconstructed temples, churches, and shrines from various faiths housed inside towering skyscrapers, and open-air religious sites like Greek-style temples and giant pyramids lining the streets. The overall atmosphere resembles a theme park of famous tourist spots more than a place of worship or study. Five-story pagodas and elevated roads closed to traffic are common sights, and deer may be seen wandering about.

Due to the high number of flammable materials, District 12 has more firefighting equipment than most areas, with a Central Firefighting Tank managed by the district as a whole. On the other hand, the district's association with the occult has drawn unwanted attention in the past, such as spiritualists attempting to bomb a stadium.

School District 23 is the largest district in Academy City, located in the easternmost part of the city. It specializes completely in aeronautics and astronautics, containing facilities for the development of civilian aircraft, fighter jets, and unmanned helicopters. Half of the district is covered by runways and satellite launch areas.

The district has an international airport open to tourists and citizens, but the rest is restricted, with the blank areas on maps indicating they are not recommended for touring. District 23 also protects the neighboring District 11, with its security robots having a direct line to summon the Six Wings attack helicopters.

Notable locations include the Air Superiority Preservation Control Center which deploys the Six Wings, the Tree Diagram Information Receival Center, the space elevator Endymion, and the memorial for the miraculous emergency landing of the Spaceplane Orion. The district also contains an enormous terminal station with extensive train, subway, monorail and bus connections.

A mass driver is an electromagnetic catapult used to accelerate and launch payloads at high speeds. It primarily consists of a path for the payload to travel down, powerful electromagnets positioned along that path, and a magnetizable holder containing the payload. The electromagnets accelerate the payload holder, which then continues on the momentum it acquired after leaving the path.

Aside from linear track types, there are also silo-type mass drivers like the one in School District 23. These fire payloads from a cylindrical space using an accelerated plasma flow, achieving velocities of over Mach 20. A single-stage launch can place a payload into orbit within ten minutes. Excess electricity remains in the barrel after firing, making it dangerous to enter immediately.

The airborne Logistic Hornets developed by Space Engage incorporate mass drivers for launching spacecraft and objects into ballistic orbits. Built around a hole in the center of their wings, linear motors build up circular acceleration before firing payloads out of a launch port on the tail wing. Though limited to ballistic trajectories, they could still deliver payloads globally within around 20 minutes.

The Ability Body Crystal, also known as Crystallized Esper Essence or simply Body Crystal, is a drug that can induce an esper to temporarily overload and gain power. It was originally created and overseen by Kihara Gensei as part of the Level 6 Shift attempt to achieve SYSTEM. 

The crystal is made by collecting, refining, and purifying the unusual quantities of neurotransmitters and hormones secreted by espers who have lost control of their powers and formed abnormal synapses. By applying the crystal to selected espers, it aims to cause an AIM Diffusion Field Resonance and a power-up to Level 6, though with dangerous side effects.

The original First Sample was a small red prism requiring a whole laboratory to properly expose espers. Later powdered and tablet versions just needed to be ingested to overload an esper. The crystal was unethically tested on Child Errors by Gensei's team under the guise of an AIM field control experiment, putting them into comas. It has since spread to the dark side and been used by the group Item to boost Takitsubo Rikou's AIM Stalker, with her deteriorating from repeated use.

Endymion, fully named Space Elevator Endymion, was a space elevator located in Academy City's School District 23. Prior to its disappearance, it was the first of its kind, built in the wake of the city's victory in the Space Elevator Construction Competition. The massive structure spiraled into the sky, with a large orbital station positioned at its peak.

The elevator had great political and magical significance due to its potential to affect the balance of power between the Magic and Science Sides. Endymion's interior housed the space hotel Heavens Canceller, an observation deck, a streaming relay station used by the idol Meigo Arisa, and the Core Room where the magician Ladylee Tangleroad enacted her spell.

During the Miracle of Endymion incident, Ladylee attempted to use the elevator together with Arisa as part of a magic spell to end her own life. However, the efforts of Kamijou Touma and others managed to counter the spell. In the end, after the explosive bolts at its base were destroyed, Endymion disappeared entirely as it drifted off into space.

The Miracle of 88 Memorial is a commemorative monument located in School District 23 of Academy City. It was donated by the Orbit Portal Company to honor the 88 survivors of the Spaceplane Orion incident, which would come to be known as the Miracle of 88.

The memorial takes the form of a black stone obelisk, erected on the very spot where the Orion made its miraculous emergency landing after a grave malfunction in space. Upon the obelisk's face is inscribed a dedication from the Orbit Portal Company to the survivors, featuring a quote from Blaise Pascal's Pensées.

The towering space elevator Endymion can be seen rising up in the background behind the memorial site, as the paved area around the obelisk once served as a runway in the lead-up to the monument's construction.

The Spaceplane Orion was an advanced passenger craft developed by Academy City's Orbit Portal Company. As the first spaceplane of its kind, Orion boasted the ability to reach orbit without the need for rocket-based launch facilities. It measured an impressive 125-130 meters in length, with a spacious fuselage and powerful engines mounted on its wings and tail.

Three years prior to the main story's first year, Orion embarked on a commemorative test flight with 88 passengers and crew, including pilot Daedalus Sequenzia and his daughter Shutaura. However, the spaceplane fell victim to sabotage by Ladylee Tangleroad, leading to the Orion incident. The craft's left engine exploded, but Daedalus managed to make an emergency landing in School District 23 at the cost of his life. This event would be named the Miracle of 88.

The highly publicized incident nearly bankrupted Orbit Portal and froze Academy City's spaceplane program. Afterward, Ladylee used her influence to buy out the company and conceal the full truth behind the miraculous survival of the Orion's passengers.

Orbit Portal was a company based in Academy City that specialized in space travel and aeronautics. Originally focused on spaceflight technology, the company poured its efforts into developing the revolutionary Spaceplane Orion. Touted as the realization of humanity's space travel dreams, Orion could reach orbit without the need for rocket launch sites.

However, the company's fortunes took a dire turn after Ladylee Tangleroad sabotaged the Orion's test flight in a bid to end her own life, causing a major accident. The craft miraculously landed safely, and the incident was publicized as the Miracle of 88, but the truth behind the 89th passenger was concealed. Orbit Portal nearly fell into bankruptcy, but Ladylee bought out the company to keep it afloat.

Under Ladylee's leadership, Orbit Portal capitalized on the Miracle of 88's publicity and permanently left the spaceflight industry. The company constructed a memorial at the Orion's crash site and shifted its business to center around the concept of "miracles". Most notably, Orbit Portal spearheaded the creation of the immense space elevator Endymion.

The Tree Diagram Information Receival Center is a facility situated in Academy City's School District 23. As the name suggests, it served as the primary point of contact for receiving data from the Tree Diagram supercomputer prior to the machine's untimely destruction.

The most prominent external feature of the center is a large satellite dish, necessary for communicating with Tree Diagram as it was physically located on the orbiting Orihime-1 satellite. Internally, the facility contains a control room filled with now-outdated technology, though still functional to a degree.

According to Misaka Mikoto, the Information Receival Center was the sole means of direct contact with Tree Diagram, capable of handling hundreds of transmissions per day between the supercomputer and the Earth-based machines. In a desperate bid to sabotage the Radio Noise Project, Mikoto infiltrated the abandoned facility, hoping to access and manipulate the Tree Diagram. However, unbeknownst to her, the satellite housing the supercomputer had already been destroyed.

The Air Superiority Preservation Control Center is a military installation located in Academy City's School District 23. It serves as the central command for defending the city's airspace and deploying aerial assets.

The center is a heavily fortified complex, ringed by defensive emplacements. Hangars adjacent to the main structure house the HsAFH-11 unmanned attack helicopters, commonly known as the Six Wings, which can be rapidly scrambled to intercept threats. The interior contains rows of computer terminals manned by uniformed personnel who constantly monitor the city's airspace.

In the event of a verified incursion or emergency, the center's staff are authorized to deploy the Six Wings for defensive missions. However, the decision to release the heavily armed aircraft is not made lightly, requiring a human operator to carefully consult a lengthy manual before connecting a final go-ahead plug into the launch system, ensuring a measured response to potential dangers.

The Ironhide Institute of Aviation Technology is a prestigious research center located adjacent to an experimental airport in Academy City's School District 23. It operates as a subsidiary facility of the airport and specializes in the development of cutting-edge aeronautical technologies. 

The institute's compound is heavily guarded, with access restricted solely to authorized personnel. A imposing mesh wire fence, standing two meters tall, surrounds the perimeter, deterring would-be intruders. Buses ferrying individuals to and from the nearby airport skirt the edges of the facility, with human drivers to prevent corporate spies from disembarking mid-route. 

Ironhide's researchers dedicate their efforts to refining existing aviation concepts and pushing the boundaries of what's possible. One of their primary focuses is advancing the design and implementation of short runway systems within the unique environment of Academy City. These innovations are then rigorously tested at the adjoining experimental airfield, cementing the institute's reputation as a leader in its field.

Academy City International Airport is the sole aviation hub for arrivals and departures into the illustrious city-state. While primarily catering to tourists and officially sanctioned visitors from outside Academy City, its services are also available to the city's own residents, such as Kamijou Touma and Index. 

The airport boasts an array of advanced facilities and equipment, standing as a testament to the cutting-edge technology that defines Academy City. Among its featured aircraft are Supersonic Passenger Planes, capable of completing direct flights to distant destinations like Italy's Marco Polo Airport in Venice with unrivaled speed and comfort.

A shopping center, brimming with an assortment of retail outlets and dining options, is conveniently situated a mere 1.5 kilometers from the airport terminal. This commercial complex, while not directly part of the airport grounds, is a popular stopover for travelers and residents alike, offering a vibrant atmosphere and a taste of the city's modern amenities.

School District 23's Terminal Station is a colossal transportation nexus that serves as the primary gateway to the district's numerous facilities and institutions. Its sheer size and passenger capacity rival those of the bustling international airport located within the same district.

The station's complex network of platforms and concourses accommodates an impressive array of rail and road-based transit options. No less than eight conventional train lines, five subterranean metro routes, a pair of high-speed monorail tracks, and four designated bus terminals converge at this sprawling hub, ensuring seamless connectivity to every corner of the district.

In addition to the standard passenger services, the terminal also features exclusive infrastructure catering to the district's more specialized needs. A secure freight rail line links directly to the station's expansive switchyard, facilitating the efficient loading, unloading, and servicing of heavy cargo trains. For the district's VIP visitors and residents, a dedicated lane provides discreet and expedited access to the terminal, separate from the general public thoroughfares.

Hikoboshi II is an advanced Academy City spy satellite, officially referred to as a weather satellite, and one of three such satellites the city possesses. The satellite is 5km long and has a module that allows it to carry out additional experiments, which can navigate separately.

Hikoboshi II is equipped with a large caliber ground-attack laser, an optical bombing weapon using white light waves to heat targets up to 4000 degrees and destroy cell nuclei. It has a firing range of 5m to 3km radius, but is limited to roughly one shot per hour and has slight accuracy issues due to atmospheric refraction.

The satellite also possesses the Magnetic Debris Cannon, which sends large masses into orbit, accelerates them with the Earth's rotational kinetic energy, then uses electromagnetism to drop them on targets. Authorization from a high-level researcher's brainwaves is needed to use this weapon. Hikoboshi II is integral to Academy City's surveillance and played a role in various incidents and conflicts throughout the series.

School District 11 is located in the southeast of Academy City, serving as the city's primary goods transfer area and can be summed up as a warehouse district. Sharing a border with the outer wall, it functions as the entrance for the land shipping route.

The district's buildings are lined up in an organized manner and resemble parking garages more so than normal structures. These garage-like buildings house Academy City-made electric cars awaiting shipment. The district has an immense 7000 ton daily material turnover capacity. Large shipping containers are repacked into smaller units for distribution throughout the city after passing customs checks.

School District 11 employs cutting-edge automation to streamline its shipping process, with nearly all work handled by machines. Engineers, some armed with handguns, are among the few on-site human staff. The area near the outer wall gate is tightly controlled, with security robots directly linked to the control area in District 23 patrolling the wall pathways.

Parallel Sweets Park is a large snack-themed amusement park located near Academy City and the Hakumeiza cinema. The park is as expansive as an electrical plant and was constructed and financed by a collaboration of four major snack manufacturers.

The park features 75 stores representing 38 countries. A unique layout of donut-shaped, interconnected waterways resembling the Olympic rings symbol runs through the park grounds. Top-quality snack shops line the outer perimeter of these circular waterways.

Within the central square encircled by the waterways, various snack makers showcase their products and host themed activities. Parallel Sweets Park is also the site of one of the 47 Portals of Japan, adding a layer of magical significance to the whimsical venue.

The Twilight Theater, known in Japanese as Hakumeiza, is an abandoned art theater situated in Eastern Tokyo approximately three kilometers from Academy City. The theater building is square-shaped and larger than a stadium, with a small parking lot at its entrance. A bus stop and multi-story parking garage are located nearby.

After its closure, the entire theater was encircled by a two-meter tall barricade of metal plates and iron bars. Remarkably, in the initial three weeks post-abandonment, none of the building's walls or glass surfaces fell victim to vandalism or breakage. The theater's entrance boasts five impressive glass doors.

Despite its state of disrepair, the Twilight Theater played a pivotal role in the story, serving as the meeting point between Stiyl Magnus, Agnese Sanctis, and Kamijou Touma during the incident surrounding the retrieval of the Book of the Law and Orsola Aquinas.

The Church of Orsola was a Roman Catholic church under construction near Academy City, named in honor of Orsola Aquinas for her efforts in spreading Christianity to three pagan nations. Had it been completed, it would have been the largest church in Japan, rivaling the size of a baseball stadium and capable of accommodating over 250 people even in its unfinished state.

The church was comprised of seven chapels, each designed to facilitate one of the Seven Sacraments. The size and grandeur of the individual chapels varied based on their liturgical importance and anticipated frequency of use, with the two largest being the Marriage Chapel and the Extreme Unction Chapel, the latter serving as the venue for funeral rites. Other chapels included the Holy Order Chapel, Confirmation Chapel, and Baptism Chapel.

The Church of Orsola was not merely a place of worship but also a tourist attraction. The Vatican had even launched a mobile-friendly website to promote the church. However, the structure was heavily damaged during the battle between the Amakusa Christians and Agnese Forces who were after Orsola Aquinas. Following Orsola's defection to the Anglican Church, the unfinished church was dismantled.

The Trial of Sin is a mock holy trial historically used by both the Church of England and the Roman Catholic Church to determine if an accused individual is a sinner and test their faith in God. Despite being banned, the Roman Catholic Church is rumored to still employ this trial on occasion.

The trial is deliberately set up in such a manner that the accused will always be found guilty, regardless of the outcome. The accused may be subjected to impossible tests, such as holding a scalding metal rod - if they are unharmed, God has protected them and proven their innocence, but if they are burned, they are guilty. Even if the accused miraculously passes the test, they will still be condemned, with the justification that the devil intervened on their behalf.

According to Stiyl Magnus, the trial can last 2-3 days before culminating in the execution of the accused. The Roman Catholic Church's version of the trial is said to involve especially appalling procedures that are far worse than those of the Anglican Church. The Agnese Forces' brutal beating of Orsola Aquinas in the Church of Orsola served as a grim simulation of what she would have endured had she been subjected to the official trial.

The Divine Protection of Ægidius is a building-level barrier spell employed by the Roman Catholic Church, named after Saint Ægidius, also known as Saint Giles. The spell can envelop a large area or structure, such as a church, using a single talisman as its focus.

While the exact effects of the Divine Protection of Ægidius are unknown, it is potent enough that a group effort is required to dispel it. As a Christian power, it is not invulnerable to the Imagine Breaker, the mysterious negating ability possessed by Kamijou Touma in his right hand.

During the events surrounding Orsola Aquinas, the Agnese Forces utilized this spell to shroud the Church of Orsola, aiming to conduct their trial of Orsola without interference. However, Touma's Imagine Breaker unexpectedly negated the barrier, catching the nuns off guard and foiling their plans.

A magic circle is a complex diagram or geometric pattern used to facilitate the casting of magic spells. The most basic form is a simple circle, but as more information is encoded into the design, the circle's power increases accordingly. Magical symbols like pentagrams, hexagrams, the Star of David, and the Seal of Solomon are often incorporated for added potency.

Other elements frequently included in magic circles are the names of angels or beings from whom power is drawn, the type and quantity of Telesma (the power source for magic), and instructions on how the energy will be wielded. The perimeter may be adorned with names and words that, under the principles of Idol Theory, further augment the circle by tapping into the power of what they represent.

However, the more intricate a magic circle becomes, the greater the difficulty in controlling it. Even the slightest misalignment between the caster's intent and the circle's configuration can lead to disastrous results, causing the spell to spiral out of control. Magic circles can be constructed on various surfaces, from simple drawings to complex three-dimensional arrangements, and can even utilize the positions of celestial bodies.

Gungnir is the legendary spear of Odin from Norse mythology, said to never miss its target when thrown. In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, it is the spiritual item coveted by the Magic God Othinus to remake the world as she sees fit. Many events surround the necessary preparations for its construction.

The true Gungnir wielded by Othinus appears as a golden spear, its shaft intertwined with a ribbon-like design. Instead of a pointed tip, it has a wide blade resembling a double-edged sword. The broad blade features an engraved branch and leaf motif. When thrown, the spear shatters the world, the fragments transforming into a massive swarm of deadly weapons that swallow the target whole.

As one of Odin's weapons, Gungnir symbolizes his authority and grants its wielder his power. It allows a magic god like Othinus to bypass her 50/50 limitation and use her full abilities to destroy, create, or alter the world at will. However, a replica or imitation of Gungnir, while immensely powerful, cannot grant a human such divine command.

Sargasso refers to various oceanic locations in the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index where sea wreckage naturally accumulates to form artificial islands. These sites arise under specific conditions - the convergence of several currents, an abundance of flotsam and driftwood, and a reef or similar structure to anchor the debris. Ships that did not completely sink, from fishing boats to military vessels, can drift over 100 kilometers to amass at these spots.

Magicians use the term Sargasso to describe these phenomenon, unrelated to the Sargasso Sea near the Gulf of Mexico. While no official records document their numbers, local fishermen continue to fear these legendary ship graveyards. Gremlin, a magic cabal in the series, utilizes Sargasso as hidden bases of operation. The organization values these sites for their ley lines, concealment from enemies, and the machinery available from the wrecked ships.

Gremlin maintains two major Sargasso bases - one in the North Sea near Iceland and another serving as their main headquarters in Tokyo Bay. The Tokyo Bay location is protected by magical creatures known as Muspells and a massive Mokkerkalfe construct. Despite their remote nature, these Sargasso bases play a pivotal role in Gremlin's nefarious plans and the story's events.

Mokkerkalfe, also known as Mökkurkalfe, is a giant made of clay that appears in Norse mythology to aid the giant Hrungnir in his battle against Thor. In legend, it was an artificial construct with a mare's heart encased within a mountainous form sculpted from clay. However, the heart made Mokkerkalfe so cowardly that it was unable to properly fight, and Thor's servant ultimately destroyed it.

In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, this myth forms the basis for at least two different spells. The first is the Mokkerkalfe of Buckingham Palace, a spiritual item crafted to safeguard a hidden tunnel and railway car linked to the Curtana Original. Initially disguised as a wall adorned with a poster, it transformed into a giant composed of paper upon detection of intruders. This version was optimized using British magical theories.

The second is the Mokkerkalfe employed by the magic cabal Gremlin. More akin to the original myth, it manifested as a colossal giant of dried clay, large enough to disrupt ley lines. Controlled remotely through a heart-like device in Gremlin's Tokyo Bay Sargasso base, it emerged from the ocean depths to intercept enemies and buy time for Gungnir's construction. This Mokkerkalfe was under the command of the Gremlin magician Freyja.

Marian Slingeneyer is a core member of the magic cabal known as Gremlin. She is a Dvergr, a mythical dwarven craftsman, with the ability to recreate weapons from Norse legends. Vital to Gremlin's plans, Marian is one of the first true members of the group introduced in the story.

In appearance, Marian is a young woman with dark skin, silver braided hair, and circular earrings. She wears work gloves and overalls adorned with the crest of Jörmungandr, the World Serpent of Norse myth, often without undergarments. Despite her carefree attitude towards her revealing attire, Marian displays a sadistic side, brutally using her powers on enemies.

Marian's magic allows her to reshape living human bodies into tools, furniture, and weapons, keeping them alive in their new forms. She can also summon these transformed victims through conduits like her gold accessories. As a Dvergr, Marian played a key role in Gremlin's attempt to build the legendary spear Gungnir for their leader, the Magic God Othinus. She shared a close bond with her partner Kihara Kagun, and after his death and Othinus' betrayal, Marian turned against her former leader in a quest for revenge.

Kihara Kagun, also known by the alias Bersi, was a former member of the infamous Kihara family and a key figure in the magic cabal Gremlin. Knowledgeable in both science and magic, he played a pivotal role in the group's machinations, using his expertise to help them combine the two disciplines.

Kagun had a lean, almost androgynous build and short, slightly spiky black hair. During his time with Gremlin, he concealed his identity with a white coat, gloves, shoes, and a distinctive white helmet. Underneath, his eyes were a piercing black.

As a Kihara, Kagun possessed a natural affinity for science and a tendency towards amoral actions. However, he managed to overcome his dark upbringing, becoming a magician and even a teacher who genuinely cared for his students. His past eventually caught up with him in the form of a tragic incident orchestrated by a fellow Kihara. Seeking revenge, Kagun joined Gremlin and began studying magic, focusing on spells designed to counter his nemesis. His primary magical ability was the use of the Whitting, a sword that grew stronger with every attack it endured, symbolizing his own resilience.

Tokyo, the capital and largest city of Japan, serves as the primary real-world setting for much of the Toaru series. Officially known as the Tokyo Metropolis, it is a vast urban center on the eastern coast of Honshu, the main island of Japan. Tokyo is a bustling, modern city known for its cutting-edge technology, vibrant pop culture, and unique blend of traditional and contemporary architecture.

In the world of Toaru, Tokyo is notable for housing the independent city-state of Academy City. This advanced scientific enclave, home to a population of espers and host to a wide array of research institutions, occupies a substantial portion of the Tokyo Metropolitan Area's western half. The interaction and contrast between the normalcy of Tokyo and the extraordinary nature of Academy City form a core theme of the series.

Throughout the story, various locations in Tokyo outside of Academy City play host to significant events. Districts such as Shinjuku and Shibuya are common setting for the Urban Legends story arcs. Other important sites include a certain iron railway bridge over a river and the Twilight Theater. These areas in Eastern Tokyo often become battlegrounds for conflicts between the Magic and Science Sides.

School District 14 is located in the northeast corner of Academy City, adjacent to the city of Saitama. Like its neighbor School District 3, the district is notable for catering to outsiders. However, where District 3 focuses more on accommodating visitors and tourists, District 14 specializes in housing overseas students.

The district's dormitories and facilities are designed to cater to the needs of foreign transfer students. Its architecture is a diverse blend of styles from around the world, with high-tech skyscrapers standing alongside smaller blocks featuring Italian, Chinese, Korean, and Indian designs. The residential areas are divided by the students' cultural backgrounds, and guide plates on the dormitories often feature languages other than Japanese.

School District 14 has been the site of several significant events throughout the series. During the Necromancer Arc, it was a key location in the conflict surrounding Esther Rosenthal and the Hishigata sisters. One year prior to the main story, it was also where Item ambushed the underground Meltdowner research lab of Hula Hoop, shortly before a raid by the criminal organization Honey Queen.
