As a covert unit, the Freshmen operatives are produced and maintained in secret bases throughout Academy City, located in blind spots of the city's advanced surveillance network. They resent the Graduates who they see as their inferiors but were still treated as superior to them.

The Freshmen were involved in the hunt for Fremea Seivelun, clashing with Accelerator and Hamazura Shiage. It would later be revealed this was part of Yakumi Hisako's plan to test and induce Agitate Halation in the girl, with the Freshmen luring both Level 5 and Level 0 into the conflict.

Silvercross Alpha is a member of the Freshmen organization known for his large collection of powered suits. Originally he had a graceful face, but it was burned off as punishment in the past, leaving him with a twisted mentality focused on adapting his mind and body to pilot his many suits. After regaining his original looks, Silvercross feels no attachment to his own body or appearance.

His primary suit is the small armadillo-like Life Armor, which he uses to leap between his larger custom suits during battle. These include the 8-legged gun platform Enemy Blaster, the high-speed quadrupedal Highway Cheetah, and the FIVE_Over mech. Silvercross changes his mindset to match his current suit, such as thinking as a four or eight-legged creature.

Even near death, Silvercross' modified body can continue fighting on pure reflex and programming. His Emergency suit can bypass the destruction of his organic parts and puppet his corpse with artificial components. Despite cleverly exploiting his lack of unity between mind, body and tech, Silvercross was still defeated by the likes of Accelerator and Hamazura Shiage.

The Bee Launcher is one of the many specialized powered suits employed by the Freshmen operative Silvercross Alpha. This large suit is designed for reconnaissance and information gathering rather than direct combat.

The Bee Launcher's main body has a humanoid shape with a huge sensor dome for a head, two arms and two legs. Its standout feature is the twelve large poles extending from its back, each capable of storing up to ten smaller robots known as Edge Bees, for a total complement of 120.

The launch poles double as high-precision antenna, able to receive video feeds from the deployed Edge Bees and intercept signals from machines across Academy City. The suit can also link into communication networks and security systems using direct cable connections.

Despite not being a frontline combat suit, the Bee Launcher possesses significant physical strength, enough to launch a car into the air with a single blow. It is also equipped with emergency escape functions to jettison Silvercross to safety if the suit is compromised or destroyed.

The Highway Cheetah is a high-speed powered suit developed by Academy City, used by the Freshmen operative Silvercross Alpha. With a sleek design built for velocity, it is intended to rapidly transport a target and evade pursuers.

The Highway Cheetah's body is modeled after a four-legged animal, with a set of wheels and a powerful rear-mounted propeller engine, giving it the capability to "slide" across the ground at speeds up to 800 kilometers per hour. It secretes a special Slip Oil from its limbs to reduce friction, though the oil is engineered to leave no residue that could be tracked.

The suit's movements are highly monotonous and efficient, allowing them to be easily automated by the pilot through pre-programmed routes. It is outfitted with sensors and lenses on both the front and back of its frame to maintain full awareness of its surroundings.

By dynamically repositioning its legs to match any terrain, the Highway Cheetah can traverse areas with large hills, drops and narrow passageways that would be impossible for normal vehicles. Silvercross used this suit to kidnap Fremea Seivelun and escape from the monstrous Accelerator.

The Enemy Blaster is a military-grade powered suit developed by Academy City and modified for use in the Freshmen's attack on Hattori Hanzou and Fremea Seivelun. It has an unconventional design with eight legs and no distinct head, instead mounting various lenses and sensors including a radar receiver directly on the main body.

For armaments, the Enemy Blaster carries a heavy machine gun on the left arm, firing 18mm rounds at 300 per minute, and a tank-sized smoothbore gun on the right. The smoothbore gun can utilize armor-piercing fin-stabilized discarding sabot (APFSDS) rounds to punch through and shred a target's insides with shrapnel, adhesive air stun rounds to attack through walls, and canister shot.

While powerful, the Enemy Blaster was designed for a warzone environment and has weaknesses in urban conditions. Its advanced sensors and targeting computers are less effective in the chaotic electromagnetic landscape of a city. This flaw was exploited by Hanzou, who realized the pilot was not actually trying to kill them.

Private salons are rentable rooms located in Academy City's School District 3, often used as hideouts by the dark side group Item. These rooms can be hired for a set time to engage in private recreational activities away from prying eyes.

The appeal of private salons lies in their ability to act as a haven for Academy City's highly regimented youth population. Students living in monitored dorms and under constant adult supervision find the salons to be a secret refuge where they can act freely, though guardians and teachers are wary of the potential for illicit activities.

Private salons come furnished with amenities such as kitchenettes, refrigerators, and entertainment systems including TVs with satellite and internet access as well as video game consoles. They may also feature recreational facilities like indoor swimming pools, showers and locker rooms. Access is restricted to salon members, with individual rooms available for reservation on a yearly contract to those with a two-star membership.

School District 3 is the northernmost district in Academy City, located adjacent to the wall bordering Saitama Prefecture. Its primary purpose is to accommodate authorized outsiders visiting the city, with a focus on hospitality and promotional industries. The district contains a number of international exhibition halls to showcase Academy City's cutting-edge technology to guests.

District 3 offers the highest standard hotels and facilities in the city, with a direct railroad line from School District 23 to allow quick access for foreign visitors. Many celebrities tend to gather here, with special amenities like ethanol car fuel blends being available to distinguish the upper class.

Besides hotels and convention centers, the district is also known for its rentable private salons. These rooms serve as secret havens for Academy City's student population to relax and socialize away from the strict regulation and oversight of their daily lives, though this has also raised concerns about potential illicit activities. District 3 also contains a large underground shopping mall.

Index Librorum Prohibitorum, commonly known as Index, is a young nun under the care of Necessarius, the 0th Parish of the Anglican Church. She has the appearance of a small 14-15 year old girl with long silver hair and green eyes, and she wears a white nun's habit with gold highlights.

Index was specifically chosen to become a vessel to hold 103,000 magical grimoires. She has the ability of Perfect Memory, allowing her to perfectly memorize all the magical knowledge without being adversely affected. However, this puts a great strain on her mind. To prevent her from dying, her memory has been forcibly erased each year, with her caretakers lying that her brain can only hold a year's worth of memories.

Index is a kind and innocent girl, but can be childish, bratty and energetic at times. She has a huge appetite. While she cannot use magic normally, she has the ability of Spell Intercept which can disrupt enemies' magic, and her knowledge grants her keen analytical abilities. She also has a hidden ability called John's Pen that activates subconsciously in emergencies, temporarily giving her access to her grimoire library. Is almost never seen without Touma's cat, Sphynx.

The Collar, also known as the Necklace, was a powerful magical spell that was placed on Index Librorum Prohibitorum by Laura Stuart of the Anglican Church. It took the form of the astronomical symbol of Jupiter drawn inside Index's mouth.

The true purpose of the Collar was to kill Index within a year if her memory was not erased, ensuring the Church would retain control over her and the 103,000 grimoires she held. It did this by slowly and painfully destroying her body and mind. The Church lied to Index and her caretakers that her brain could not hold more than a year's memories due to the grimoires, in order to justify the annual memory erasure.

The Collar was linked to Index's John's Pen mode defense system. If the Collar itself was removed or destroyed, John's Pen would activate and attempt to reconstruct it from knowledge in the grimoire library. However, it was unable to overcome the Imagine Breaker possessed by Touma Kamijou. Touma ultimately destroyed the Collar completely, freeing Index from the Church's control.

Norse mythology is one of the most prevalent magic systems in the world of A Certain Magical Index, second only to Christianity. It is based on the traditional stories of the gods, giants and heroes of pre-Christian Scandinavia.

Many different magicians and magic groups utilize Norse Mythology in their magic, including the magic god Othinus and her group GREMLIN. Norse gods like Thor and Odin are frequently referenced, and their weapons like Gungnir and Mjölnir are replicated as powerful magical artifacts. Mythological creatures like Jörmungandr and Fenrir have also appeared. 

An important aspect of Norse Mythology as portrayed in the series is that its gods are not perfect or all-powerful, but can be killed, especially in the prophesied Ragnarök. Magicians exploit this fact to find weaknesses in Norse Magic. Additionally, there are suggestions that Othinus herself may be the original basis for myths about Odin. Overall, Norse Mythology is a rich source of symbolism and power for magicians in the Indexverse.

Necessarius, also known as the Church of Necessary Evil, is the secret 0th Parish of the Church of England. It was established to counter and destroy the rampant magic and magicians in England. Despite being part of a church, all of its members are skilled magicians themselves, using magic to subdue magic.

Necessarius is known for its complex structure, incorporating many different sects and factions within it, each with their own magical specialties and religious views. This diversity allows them to tackle a wide variety of magical threats. Major groups within Necessarius include the main Anglican Church, the Amakusa-Style Remix of Church, the Roman Catholic London Branch, and others.

As an organization, Necessarius is feared and respected for its mastery of inquisition, torture, and anti-magic techniques. It has a major voice within the Church of England and significant international reach and influence. Many of Touma Kamijou's allies in the Magic Side are members of or affiliated with the Church of Necessary Evil.

Richard Brave is a 20-year-old former member of Necessarius and an antagonist in certain side stories. He has about the same height and skin color as Stiyl Magnus, and wears a black coat.

He is a selfish man completely dedicated to his work, particularly his signature spell Lævateinn, which he considers his life's greatest achievement. When the spell was deemed illegal by the Anglican Church, his pride couldn't handle it and he grew to hate the church, eventually leading him to turn against it.

Richard Brave's primary magic is his Lævateinn spell, which produces powerful red flames that can burn almost anything. The spell's secret is that it first spreads an invisible flammable substance in rune shapes, then ignites it with UV rays. He also uses mental interference magic in combat. As a magician he specializes in defensive ocean battles, and previously helped defend England from invasion by American cabals.

Brunhild Eiktobel is a character introduced in the Kanzaki SS side story as the main antagonist. She has the appearance of a beautiful girl with long blonde hair and white skin around 18 years old. Her outfit is a mix of modern and medieval European styles resembling armor.

She has a very caring personality towards her loved ones and is utterly merciless to her enemies. Brunhild is driven by a desire for revenge against those who destroyed her cabal and hurt an innocent child, as well as saving that child from a coma. She is very focused on her goals and willing to go to great lengths to achieve them.

Brunhild has the unique trait of being born as both a Saint and a Valkyrie. While this grants her immense powers like supersonic speed and extreme strength, she cannot use both sides at once as they cancel each other out and go through periodic flux. She wields a large claymore and uses Rune Magic to achieve various effects like planting runes in an enemy's body to impede their healing.

A Valkyrie is a type of magician aligned with Norse Mythology. In legends they are celestial warrior maidens that guide the souls of heroes to the afterlife. Modern magical interpretations see them as either normal humans who become superhuman through Odin's blessing or people born with the right qualities.

Valkyries are highly associated with the dead and the afterlife, possessing many abilities relating to souls and necromancy. They are also known for having immense physical abilities on par with Saints. Some Valkyries are known to be able to fall in love with humans, going to extreme lengths for the sake of their loved ones.

There are a number of different spells and magical techniques to turn a person into an "artificial valkyrie" without the need for natural talent or divine intervention. These are generally considered lesser to a true natural or blessed Valkyrie but still powerful.

In Norse Mythology, Einherjar are warriors who died in battle and were resurrected to live in Valhalla. In the modern magic system, Einherjar are dead humans who have been resurrected as a kind of magically animated corpse, apparently through the insertion of gold in key points of the body.

The resulting Einherjar maintain the skills, abilities and personality they had in life but must constantly be supplied with magical energy from an external source to function. They do not decompose and can pass for living humans, though their behavior may be "off". The magic god Othinus is a master of this spell.

The most notable Einherjar is Bersi, the resurrected form of Kihara Kagun. As an Einherjar he displays extreme resilience and the ability to operate without fatigue, while maintaining the deadly skills he possessed in life, though coming across as an emotionless machine.

Taoism is a Chinese religion and philosophy centered around the concept of the Tao, or "the Way". It teaches that all things come from and return to a primordial state of emptiness, and that suffering arises from resisting this natural flow.

Important concepts in Taoism include Yin and Yang, two opposing but complementary forces that arise from the Tao and shape all of reality, as well as the pursuit of effortless action, simplicity, humility and harmony with nature. Taoist practices include meditation, feng shui, and various rituals and spells to attain longevity or immortality.

In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, Taoism is one of the major sources of magical knowledge alongside religions like Christianity and Buddhism. Taoist Magic often involves the invocation of various Chinese gods, immortals and spirits, the use of talismans and magic circles, and the refinement of the body's energies. For example, the Taoist magician Ouma uses a formation involving the five elements to extract the powerful spiritual item Baopuzi from Index's mind.

The Jeans Slasher is an unnamed character who appears in one of the side stories as an antagonist to Kanzaki Kaori. She is a beautiful young woman around 18 years old with long silver-blonde hair. Her outfit is extremely revealing, consisting of a few pieces of armor over a bikini-like garment, elbow gloves and thigh-high boots with cow-print patterns.

She has a very flirtatious, seductive and sadistic personality, deliberately using her attractiveness to manipulate men. Her goal is to gather a large group of powerful "Einherjar" warriors by seducing men and stealing their strength. To this end she has been literally slashing the jeans off of random male passersby, an act which caught the attention of Necessarius.

As a Valkyrie, the Jeans Slasher has superhuman strength and speed and is a highly skilled swordswoman, able to exchange blows with Kanzaki. Her unique magic is called "Nine Support" which allows her to split her shadow into nine copies that attach themselves to a target that is attracted to her and control their body.

Dragons are mythical creatures found in many stories around the world. In Western stories, they tend to be depicted as evil, fire-breathing monsters that hoard treasure and are slain by heroes. In Eastern stories, they are more benevolent and associated with water, rain, and the cardinal directions.

In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, "dragon" is a term that shows up in various contexts. It is the codename used for the mysterious being known as Aiwass. References are also made to the various saints who defeated dragons in Christian tales, such as St. George, St. Martha and St. Margaret.

Dragons play a more direct role in some story arcs. A transparent dragon head appeared from Touma's severed arm stump twice - once when fighting Aureolus Izzard, and once when fighting Misaka Mikoto. Several feathered dragons also emerged from his arm in the fight against Mikoto, and one of them, the Angel Dragon, later returned by merging with the Kimi.

The Banner of the West is a symbolic weapon used in modern Western magic. It consists of an equilateral triangle with a cross in its center. When deployed, it protects the user by monitoring for and rejecting any "evil" power approaching the area, while letting through "good" or "useful" power.

The Banner is considered one of the most useful and convenient symbolic weapons because it distinguishes between wanted and unwanted supernatural phenomena. When Aleister Crowley used it against Coronzon, he recited a chant describing how it severs ties to evil through the dual symbols and color scheme, how he need not leave his location as he is blameless, and thus the evil one must remove itself according to its sin.

Elements are artificial life forms created by Kihara Yuiitsu which invaded Academy City during a December heat wave. Their bodies are composed of translucent crystal arranged in the shape of an animal or plant, often a predatory or camouflaged one. They are animated by a magic-based core that glows with the color of one of the four classical elements - red for fire, blue for water, green for wind, yellow for earth.

Elements are highly dangerous, with great strength and the ability to bend the rules of biology. They can keep moving even when damaged in ways that would kill a normal creature. Each type has powers related to its associated element. They are also skilled at camouflage and ambush. However, they are weak to extreme heat and cold, and vulnerable to Imagine Breaker, which can destroy their cores and bodies with a touch.

The Elements were guided into Academy City by a giant Crystal Tower. Different classes of Element vary in size from 3 meters to over 100 meters. They are not sapient, but can follow simple commands, such as to congregate in one place or to self-destruct. After Yuiitsu was defeated, she had the remaining Elements kill themselves.

The Black World is an alternate state of reality created by the magic god Othinus after she obtained her special spear, Gungnir. It is a world of utter nothingness, without land, sea, sky, stars or living things. Only a perfectly flat black surface stretches out infinitely in all directions.

The Black World served as a kind of blank slate or loading screen that Othinus would call up between making changes to the world. She would drop Touma into it while crafting a new reality to break his spirit. It was the only thing that remained after she destroyed the world with Gungnir.

Despite being empty of matter and light, the Black World has a breathable atmosphere and normal gravity, presumably due to Othinus' power. It played a key role during Touma and Othinus' final battle, where Othinus turned it into her crossbow to attack him after losing Gungnir.

The Knights of England are one of the three great powers in the United Kingdom alongside the British Royal Family and the Anglican Church. Their mission is to maintain the balance of power between the three factions. In the past, the knights used specialized titles related to weapons like lances, maces and axes, but abandoned this system after mastering all knight techniques.

The knights are a formidable fighting force, inheriting techniques from the Crusaders that have defeated many other religious factions. When empowered by the Curtana, their power is so great they could make an island disappear. They use an official model of armor which channels magic to increase mobility and toughness.

While technically equal to the other powers, there are tensions with the church, who the knights see as a tool that shouldn't restrict them. They dislike taking orders from the Archbishop and will sometimes even disobey. Ultimately, the knights are loyal to the Queen above all else.

Holegres Mirates is an English nobleman and one of the Knights of England. He has the appearance of an overweight, middle-aged man clad in outdated, jewel-encrusted silk clothing beneath his armor.

Holegres is corrupt and self-serving, seeking to use his position to increase his own wealth and influence, even if it means exploiting a crisis. He takes pride in his noble status but lacks the chivalry and courage expected of a knight, staying away from direct combat. He also holds racist views, seeing outsiders as parasites draining the country's resources.

During the invasion of the UK, Holegres oversaw the defenses of London and tried to use the situation to advance his agenda by claiming the authority of the royals. He was eventually confronted and defeated by Accelerator. His armor was tough enough to withstand several of Accelerator's attacks.

The Female Knight is an unnamed member of the Knights of England. She has long, wavy blonde hair and wears silver armor with a maroon surcoat decorated with gold.

She has a serious and straightforward personality, with a strong sense of justice and duty as a knight. However, she is not entirely without empathy, showing concern for enemies and targets. It's speculated she may have had a sheltered upbringing, being a bit naive and awkward with men outside of the knights.

The Female Knight is a skilled swordswoman and horse rider, capable of acting as a commander for knight forces. She wields a steel sword that can transform into a giant spear of light, and a regular crossbow. During the invasion of the UK, she fought against the Crowley's Hazards forces but was overwhelmed by an enemy that transformed into a giant octopus.

Alex is a male horse belonging to Second Princess Carissa. He is a muscular horse outfitted with armor and military gear.

Alex was raised and trained to be a royal horse and steed. He is said to only grow attached to pure maidens, though not to the extreme degree of unicorns in legends. While Carissa was imprisoned, she entrusted Alex's care to the Female Knight.

Being a horse trained for military and official duties, Alex has enhanced strength and stamina. He is equipped with special horseshoes for running on urban terrain and can keep up with vehicles like motorcycles. Several magical spells were used on him during his training.

Aleister Crowley is a mysterious and powerful magic user, acclaimed as the greatest magician in history. He has an androgynous appearance, being a tall man with long silver hair and golden eyes. Originally the Academy City Board Chairman and ruler of the Science Side, he is eventually revealed to have a higher dimensional existence, having absorbed many of his alternate possibilities.

Aleister is a schemer and chessmaster, manipulating events from behind the scenes according to his own plan. While extremely cynical and willing to sacrifice lives for his goals, his ultimate objective is to make the world a better place. He rejects becoming a Magic God and works to remain "human", in his own way. Aleister can be ruthless to his enemies but has a certain respect for Kamijou Touma.

Aleister is a master of many forms of magic, with his primary combat magic being Spiritual Tripping. This magic links him to a target and forces images of weapons into their mind to manifest illusionary weapons with real effects. He also wields the Blasting Rod, which amplifies his magic, and has the Archetype Controller, allowing him to manipulate the underlying common images in people's minds. He can use Karma to guide and bind targets. Other magic he uses includes complex Thelema-based spells, blood sacrifices, curse  reversal and Christian Magic.

Wax magic refers to magic that uses wax for spells. The most well-known form is making a wax doll in the likeness of a target and putting some of their hair or nails in it, allowing the user to curse them by damaging the doll. This is a type of Infection Magic, similar to Voodoo dolls or Japan's Ushi no Koku Mairi.

There are also many legends about corpse wax, produced from human remains. Items like the Hand of Glory are made from a dead prisoner's arm turned to corpse wax as a candlestick said to bring good luck. Necessarius and Dusk Waiting to Awaken use blood red corpse wax infused with a witch's potion to guard their labyrinth and attack intruders. The wax can change shape, identify targets with their blood, and attack in hard to evade ways.

Other uses of wax magic include the Amakusa Christians making a perfect wax disguise of Flack Anchors to allow Itsuwa to infiltrate Necessarius. Magicians like Torquay Shadowmint can also use miniatures like wax dolls and small bells to remotely control or represent larger targets as part of various spells.

The Sword Sanctuary is a Necessarius facility specializing in the care, storage, customization, and retuning of powerful and dangerous spiritual items. While the building appears unremarkable from the outside, most of the complex is underground, expanded chaotically like an ant colony. There are few facilities for people, reflecting its focus on spiritual items over human occupants.

One of the Sword Sanctuary's key roles is to retune spiritual items that are so powerful they risk harming their wielders, making them safer to use. This allows the facility to keep heretical items with the justification of letting people vent frustrations over such objects being kept from them. The sanctuary has a large underground document room with countless files on magic side incidents, and a morgue used to analyze spiritual item wounds on corpses.

Notable items kept in the Sword Sanctuary include Hrungnir, a massive stone club on a cart that can break any barrier in one explosive blow at the cost of harming the wielder, and an experimental suit of armor that recklessly boosts the wearer's magic by tapping their life force directly. The Sanctuary's bell towers can also be used as part of a powerful long-range bombardment spell.

A curse is a type of magic cast to bring harm or misfortune to a target. There are various methods to cast curses, often using Infection Magic with a symbolic link to the target like blood, hair or a wax/straw doll. These are seen in practices worldwide like Voodoo. Substances associated with pollution like mud or animal blood are also used.

Countless curses fueled by resentment and jealousy fly around the world like invisible bullets. There are also many cursed items said to bring misfortune to their owners, like certain jewels and precious metals which are thought to invite envy. Cursed swords that can only be healed by a paired jewel are another recurring type.

The famous Abracadabra incantation is used in curse reversal spells to reflect curses back at enemies. Aleister Crowley developed a technique to hijack passing curses and redirect them at his targets. He has also inflicted other curses, like ones said to make the magicians he defeated in the Golden Dawn suffer constant failure afterwards. Other magic users like Yamisaka Ouma have motivations tied to saving others from curses.

keys: Distortion of the Laws of the World
entries.content:
The Distortion of the Laws of the World refers to an event of unknown cause that occurred before the start of the Angel Fall arc, with effects going unnoticed for some time. According to Fiamma of the Right, the distortion created 'holes' that allowed events like Angel Fall to occur in the first place.

The distortion affected the very laws of the world, including the four classical elements of Earth, Water, Wind and Fire. Most notably, it caused the elemental alignments of the four Archangels to change - Uriel, aligned with Earth, took on the element of Wind, while the others were similarly affected. Additionally, the Archangels were able to choose new names for themselves, no longer bound by the names given to them by God.

Fiamma of the Right addressed the event directly when fighting Vento of the Front, noting how the angel she was aligned with, Uriel, was meant to hold the element of Earth rather than Wind. He stated it was a serious issue requiring immediate attention. Fiamma would later create the Star of Bethlehem for a number of purposes, one being to restore the elemental balance so that his Holy Right would be perfectly aligned with Michael. The distortion was eventually undone through the use of Christian symbolism and the Star of Bethlehem.
entries.comment: Distortion of the Laws of the World

entries.content:
The Hopping Zombie spell is a magic spell originating from Taoism that manipulates the dead. It is grouped together with other magic related to manipulating the dead such as Necromancy, Hand of Glory and Vetala Sorcery.

The name of the spell references the Jiangshi (僵尸) of Chinese legends and folklore. These are a type of reanimated corpse which hide in the day in dark places like coffins and caves, then move around at night by hopping with outstretched arms. They kill living creatures to absorb their life essence. 

While the exact form and mechanics of the Hopping Zombie spell are unknown, it can be assumed to involve reanimating a corpse as a Jiangshi under the caster's control. The spell was one of the elements which the Rosenthal Family head Isaac combined with their Necromancy to develop into the Rosenthal-style several hundred years ago.

The Hand of Glory is a magic artifact involving a dried and pickled hand, usually the left hand, of a hanged man. According to European folklore, when a candle made from the fat of the same man was placed upon it, the Hand of Glory gained the power to render anyone who saw its light motionless, as well as the ability to unlock any door.

In old tales, the hand specifically had to come from a hanged murderer and would be the hand that 'did the deed'. The legends surrounding the Hand have led to it being grouped together with other magic involving the dead such as Necromancy, Vetala Sorcery, the Hopping Zombie spell and the Elixir of Life.

While the Hand of Glory has been referenced in relation to other death-related magic, its exact capabilities in practice are unknown.

The Elixir of Life, also known as the Elixir of Immortality or simply the Elixir, is a legendary alchemical potion said to grant the drinker eternal life and youth. While humanity has sought such an elixir throughout history, its true existence is unconfirmed.

In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, alchemists are traditionally attributed with the ability to create such elixirs to attain immortality, though its difficulty or limitations can be inferred from how alchemists also pursue other methods such as the secrets of vampires. Immortality is a means for alchemists to eventually achieve Ars Magna, the simulation of the world within the mind.

Various individuals throughout history such as St. Germain and Ayton of the Golden Dawn have claimed or been reputed to have created an Elixir of Life. However, many of these claims are dubious and likely false. The Rosicrucian Order has legends referencing an immortality-granting drug. The Water of Life and Death, featured in a Russian tale, is a conceptually similar substance that grants and takes life.

St. Germain is an enigmatic and legendary figure in the magical world, said to have appeared throughout medieval Europe at various points in history, traversing social circles and accruing knowledge. Accounts paint him as an ageless man of many talents, from alchemy and jewel repair to an unaging immortal who required nothing but water, pills and wheat to survive. However, much of his background is uncertain and subject to speculation, with no definitive records of birth, death or lineage.

While the legends are false, the identity of St. Germain nevertheless took on a life of its own, becoming a sort of con that magicians could use to manipulate nobles and acquire resources. Eventually this gave rise to an actual St. Germain - a collective identity and crystalline thought network spread between multiple individuals through infection with a specific ideology via pills containing microbes. Each member believes themself to be the 'real' St. Germain, with no true central unit and the group as a whole comprising the full identity.

While St. Germain's plans and goals are muddled by contradictions arising from the group's nature, they possess formidable capabilities. Notably, through the spiritual item Chambord and knowledge from legends of St. Germain repairing jewels, they can manipulate carbon in myriad ways, shaping it into spears and beasts or melting it down. The Chambord also allows St. Germain to spread the microbes that enable others to join the network, with pills used to stabilize new or errant units.

Ambrosia is a small magical fruit, cone-like in appearance, that bestows ageless immortality upon the consumer, forever preserving them in the state they were when they ate it. The effects are powerful, staving off not only death from aging, but from any other cause, be it mundane or supernatural, as experienced by Ladylee Tangleroad.

However, this immortality comes at a price - one who has eaten ambrosia may never use magic on their own, as it disrupts the cycles of life force within them that are necessary to work magic. As such, anyone who has gained immortality through ambrosia must rely on others to use magic for them.

It is unknown if the power of the Imagine Breaker would be capable of negating the effects of eating ambrosia. The fruit is named after the divine food of the Greek gods, said to confer immortality in myth, and conceptually it bears similarities to other immortality-granting items in legend such as the Elixir of Life.

A Secret Chief is a type of transcendental being spoken of in the traditions of the Golden Dawn and Rosicrucian Order. Distinct from yet similar to Magic Gods, they are superhuman entities of great magical skill and knowledge who are claimed to guide humanity from the shadows. Some state that the Secret Chiefs must approve the founding of any magical cabal.

Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers described the Secret Chiefs as having the appearance of one who had drunk the Elixir of Life. They are associated with the highest levels of the Golden Dawn. The magician Anna Sprengel acts as a priestess and point of contact for them, able to communicate with the Secret Chiefs and wield their power at will, putting her in a unique position.

The only being concretely identified as a Secret Chief so far is Aiwass, the transcendent 'angel' entity who contacted Aleister Crowley in 1904 and provided him with the Book of the Law. Originating from the deepest layer of reality, Aiwass requires a vessel to fully manifest and wield power on the surface. Aiwass is closely tied to Aleister's Aeon of Horus and the systems of Magick developed from his contact with it.

Vetala Sorcery is a form of magic relating to the manipulation of the dead and is grouped together with Necromancy and the Hopping Zombie spell. The term Vetala refers to a ghost-like being from Hindu mythology which possesses and inhabits corpses, using them as vehicles to move around. They can control these bodies and keep them from decaying, but may also exit them at will.

The exact capabilities and mechanics of Vetala Sorcery as it appears in the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index are unknown, but given its association with other magic involving manipulating the dead, it likely involves controlling corpses in a manner similar to the mythological Vetala.

Bisai Otome is an antagonist who led a research project on the Attached Microbes. She is described as a young woman around the age of Kamijou Touma, but with an oddly sexy appearance. She wears a blazer from some school that looks unnatural on her.

Despite her youth, Otome is an Academy City professor in charge of experiments and has her own security detail. Her goal was to retrieve the Martian Microbes and create similar microbes on Earth by replicating the environment of Mars in the Mars World experiment. However, though the microbes she created could survive, they lacked the calculation abilities of the Martian ones.

Otome is an esper of unknown level. She uses technology such as Stun Grenades in combination with her ability, which allows her to control the directionality of special particles that transmit impacts. She scatters these particles with her Stun Grenades to hide the true nature of her power. She can also spread the particles by moving her blazer like a giant fan. Her main weapon is a whip, whose range she can extend by manipulating the impact-transmitting particles.

Fleiss is a magician and member of the Golden-style magic cabal Dawn that Wipes Away Darkness. Her cabal, originating in England, is very small and little known even in its homeland. It has greatly declined due to its members' use of outdated Tattva-based magic.

Fleiss infiltrated Academy City under the pretense of preventing a worldwide threat in order to eliminate the artificial microbes in the Mars World experiment, hoping to prove her cabal's worth. She clashed with Anti-Skill and eventually met Kamijou Touma and Index, who became involved.

As a Dawn magician, Fleiss uses Tattva-based magic which involves colorizing the five elements and indirectly interfering with natural forces by mixing colors and adding complementary colors. She uses symbolic weapons in the form of plain colored cards. For example, by emphasizing the green complement to fire's red, she can control and direct flames. A contrasting red and green card together would extinguish flames by introducing vagueness.

The Attached Microbes, also known as the Martian Microbes, are supposedly an intelligent microbial lifeform native to the planet Mars. They are able to communicate in Japanese. However, they are actually artificial microbes developed as part of the scientific project Mars World.

After Bisai Otome received signals from what she believed to be Martian Microbes, she sought to retrieve them and shelter them on Earth. To investigate them, she attempted to replicate the Martian environment and evolve similar microbes.

While Otome succeeded in creating microbes that could survive in Martian conditions, they did not develop the same calculation abilities as the supposed Martian originals. Otome also raised the suspicion that someone may have been posing as the Martian Microbes, based on how information about them had leaked out.

Fairies are legendary creatures from European folklore, often depicted as magical humanoid beings closely tied to nature. In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, various legends and attributes associated with fairies are incorporated into certain magic spells and principles.

According to the character Ollerus, fairies were originally pagan gods and goddesses who were reclassified as lesser ethereal beings as Christianity spread, diminishing their stature and power in the public consciousness. While some were reframed as demons or enemies of the faith, many fairy legends allowed them to endure in a less threatening form. 

In modern times, fairies are a ubiquitous concept, featured in many stories and pop culture depictions separate from their religious roots. However, their true origins and attributes have become obscured. Magicians like Ollerus research fairies and fairy tales to gain insight into the principles behind their magic. Ollerus developed a spell to forcibly turn a target into a fairy, which he used in an attempt to counter Magic God Othinus.

Bunny Grey is a fictional British mascot character that Karasuma Fran is obsessed with. His appearance combines rabbit-like features, such as a white head with pointed ears, with elements of stereotypical 'grey' aliens like large red oval eyes, giving him a creepy yet cute aesthetic.

According to his in-universe backstory, Bunny Grey is a mischievous alien visitor to Earth who arrives after mistaking Stonehenge for a landing site and goes on to have many adventures with human companions. These escapades include investigating mysteries, making crop circles, and winding up preserved in a museum.

Fran owns a variety of Bunny Grey merchandise like hoodies, stickers and an inflatable pool. She also named her space station the Bunny Grey Messenger in his honor. Mascot costumes of the character seem to be relatively common.

Aliens, extraterrestrial life forms originating from worlds other than Earth, are a concept that has long fascinated humanity. While no concrete proof of alien life has been found, they are a staple of science fiction and feature heavily in various fictional works in the Toaru series.

Theories about certain mysterious beings like Aiwass and Fräulein Kreutune possibly being aliens have been proposed in-universe. Additionally, various occult and supernatural phenomena such as fairies, mysterious disappearances and crop circles have been attributed to or conflated with aliens in the public consciousness. 

Alien-based or themed characters and elements that have appeared include the Bunny Grey mascot, Kihara Byouri's 'Grey'-inspired transformation, and the extraterrestrial dragon concept design from the Daihaseisai incident. Overall, aliens are a recurring motif often mentioned or referenced throughout the story in various contexts.

Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, often called the 'Red Planet' due to its reddish appearance. It has long been an object of fascination and speculation regarding the possibility of extraterrestrial life.

In the world of Toaru Majutsu no Index, Mars is the supposed origin of the Attached Microbes, an allegedly alien life form that communicated with Bisai Otome on Earth, prompting her to attempt to replicate Mars' environment and create similar microbes, resulting in the Mars World experiment.

Other references to Mars include a participant in the Natural Selector claiming to communicate with Martian bacteria, the development of the cp-191 hibernation drug as part of a scrapped manned Mars mission, and the S5 supplying water and nutrients to celestial bodies like Mars for terraforming purposes.

A temple, in magical terms, is a consecrated space or magic circle that converts the raw power of the world into a usable form, generating a large amount of magical energy. Physical temples can be quickly constructed to power a specific large-scale spell, or exist as permanent structures.

Magical temples are not limited to physical buildings, and can be created from any materials using Idol Theory to establish a symbolic connection, such as arranging toy figurines, beads or books to represent a temple's layout and link them to specific concepts or targets.

Many temples also serve as fortresses, using magical traps and barriers to protect those inside and restrict access. The three major religions' headquarters are examples of such well-defended temples. Mental temples constructed within the mind, such as those used by the Blasting Rod Arts, are another form of magical temple that exists.

Immortality is a state in which one does not die from injury or age when normally expected. Exact manifestations vary, but immortals can recover from fatal wounds, are unaffected by them entirely, or simply do not age past a certain point. Theoretically, their unlimited lifespan grants access to incredible stores of magical energy and the ability to learn any spell, even ones impossible for mortals.

Various beings are said to possess immortality inherently, such as gods and vampires. It is a sought-after trait and the subject of much research throughout history. Methods to attain immortality, to varying degrees of success, include the creation of elixirs like ambrosia, vampiric infection, and following the path of magic to become a Magic God. Certain spells and weapons are capable of killing immortals under specific conditions.

Known immortals in the world of Index include the Magic Gods, Aleister Crowley, Fraulein Kreutune, St. Germain, and others who have used magical means. Notably, while ambrosia granted Ladylee Tangleroad true immortality, it also prevented her from using magic personally by warping her life force. The Imagine Breaker's effects on immortality are unknown.

William Wynn Westcott, referred to primarily as Westcott, was an elderly British coroner, magician, and one of the Three Founders of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. His magical prowess was inferior to Mathers and Crowley, but he led a powerful faction in the cabal through political influence and a form of quasi-immortality. This state was achieved by distorting his life force's circulation via a great being's attraction, with a red mass in his chest containing his soul. Details are unclear, but it involved his access to corpses, forging documents, and transferring souls via parchment.

Westcott advocated tradition and compromise over Mathers' desire for progress at any cost. Westcott also forged letters from the fictional Anna Sprengel to grant prestige to the cabal at its founding. These conflicting views and methods split the Golden Dawn into two factions. Westcott was reluctant to admit Aleister Crowley and was later struck down by him using the Imagine Breaker during the Battle of Blythe Road, despite his quasi-immortality.

Westcott wielded wax seals as weapons, using the light and force they released to attack, enhance his own movements and draw on the knowledge of the Golden Dawn's origins to empower his blows. After his death, Westcott was among the members of the Golden Dawn recreated by Coronzon to counter Aleister Crowley during the Crowley's Hazard invasion of the UK.

Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers, primarily referred to as Mathers, was a charismatic yet eccentric British magician. He was one of the Three Founders of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn and a mentor to Aleister Crowley before becoming his enemy. He always wears a colorful old Scottish military uniform with a pointed witch's hat and thick cloak, and speaks with hints of a Scottish accent.

Mathers co-founded the Golden Dawn and led it together with Westcott as it pursued a unified theory of magic. However, the two developed conflicting views on how magic and the cabal should progress. Unlike Westcott, Mathers advocated pushing forward into heretical areas to advance magic, desiring his name to be the one associated with the cabal's achievements and legacy. He invited Aleister Crowley to help him in this goal, but this backfired when Crowley rebelled, angered by Mathers' role in his daughter's future doom. Mathers was defeated by Crowley and struck down by him using Blythe Road's Treasure, the Imagine Breaker.

Mathers was an extremely powerful magician, making heavy use of the four elemental Symbolic Weapons. He could combine them to produce various powerful effects and attacks. His most feared spell was the invocation of Belzébuth, the lord of flies, to corrupt a target's body and break their spirit. Before his defeat, Mathers summoned the demon Coronzon and ordered it to guide Crowley to ruin, leaving a major mark on future events.

Mina Mathers was a British magician and painter, the wife of Golden Dawn co-founder Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers. She wore black, revealing mourning clothes with cat ears and tail, and had long white hair covered by a veil, all decorated with constellations and silver stars. This appearance was based on a recreation of her used to remind Aleister Crowley of his trauma, so it's uncertain which details matched her original look.

Mina acted as a reasonable mediator in the Golden Dawn, settling arguments between eccentric members like her husband and Westcott. However, she also displayed a witch-like tendency to tempt and tease others. She showed little love for her husband and prioritized the cabal's magical research over daily life, having to beg her friend Annie for living expenses at times. 

As an artist, Mina's skills gave form to the inspiration and ideas of the Golden Dawn's magicians, playing a key role in creating their ceremonial tools. Her most notable magical trait was an influence over cats, drawing them to her like a shadow. This was likely the source of her 'Black Cat Witch' title. In a conflict with Dion Fortune, Mina surrounded Fortune's house with black cats of various sizes which attacked and wounded her.

Allan Bennett, also known as Swami Maitrananda, was an early member of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn and a friend and mentor to Aleister Crowley. He initially had the unhealthy appearance of an old man due to a serious ailment, for which he used opium, leading to an addiction. Bennett acted as a proper mentor to Crowley, without ulterior motives unlike Mathers, making him one of the few true friends Crowley had.

Bennett was the one to inform Crowley about the future death of his daughter Lilith, due to the unintended 'sparks' produced by magic colliding with phases. He revealed the Golden Dawn founders were aware of this phenomena but continued their research regardless, believing the Blythe Road's Treasure would protect them. This drove Crowley to destroy the cabal. Bennett also gave Crowley the Blasting Rod and told him he would have to turn his fangs on himself to truly achieve his goals. 

Bennett was a skilled magician and an expert in divination, capable of accurately predicting the future using tarot cards. He was also a user of the Blasting Rod and the Spiritual Tripping technique later used by Crowley. After being cast out from the Golden Dawn and failing in life, Bennett eventually left for the East, learning yoga and Buddhism and even becoming a monk under the name Swami Maitrananda. In doing so, he ironically regained his health.

Annie Horniman was a magician of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. Her reproduced form had the appearance of an old-fashioned tutor with an old dress and a monocle. The main reason she joined the cabal was because of her best friend, Mina Mathers, who she adores to the point of admitting she would destroy the world for her if anything happened to Mina. By contrast, Annie loathes Mina's husband, MacGregor Mathers, and can't understand why her friend fell in love with him. Her thoughts and feelings show easily on her face.

As a Golden Dawn magician, Annie wields two symbolic weapons representing the pillars of Solomon's Temple -- a white club representing Jachin and a black club representing Boaz. By creating a perfect altar with her body and the two clubs, Annie can use her magic to enhance the power of other magicians with a Boost Target spell, causing a soap bubble-like distortion to appear behind her. 

Annie also possesses skill with cursing dolls and a communication spell compared to a more primitive form of astral projection, which vibrates magic power or an equivalent at a set frequency to make contact at a distance, though it isn't the most precise and can cause discomfort to others nearby.

Edward Berridge was a member of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. When magically reproduced, he took on the appearance of a military medic, wearing a plain moss-green uniform adorned with pouches containing medical supplies like bandages and disinfectant. Berridge was one of the few followers that Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers placed complete trust in.

Described by Aleister Crowley as both a magical medicine specialist and 'insurance' for the rest of the Golden Dawn, Berridge's primary tool was a reflective tablet. Using the tablet's mirror-like surface, Berridge could 'redirect' impurities and negative energies in order to magically heal others.

When the reproduced Golden Dawn confronted Aleister Crowley directly, Berridge declared that the battle would be over in five minutes, showing confidence in Mathers and the rest of the cabal. However, that confidence was misplaced. Later, when Mathers was in danger from an orbital laser attack, Berridge selflessly tackled his master out of the beam's path, and was destroyed himself, revealing the fabricated nature of the 'revived' Golden Dawn.

Frederick Leigh Gardner was an English stock broker and occultist who became a member of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. The magically reproduced version of Gardner wore old-fashioned tennis apparel consisting of a thick long-sleeved shirt and loose trousers. As a follower of the Golden Dawn's 'Lady of the Masquerade Ball', Gardner had no qualms about sacrificing personnel for larger goals and did not show a rebellious streak.

Like other members of the secret society, Gardner was a practitioner of the cabal's unique magic. He wielded a handheld oil lamp which could produce massive plumes of illusionary fire. By swinging the lamp, Gardner could shape the flames into a large Symbol of Mercury - an emblem depicting a crescent moon, circle and cross, representing all the Sephiroth except for Keter.

Gardner used an incantation to empower the fiery symbol as a weapon, causing it to unleash a blinding flash of light, shatter, and afflict a target's eyes with painful dilation. This technique was used to destroy a magical light spear and neutralize its wielder. The illusionary fire could also be reshaped for other purposes.

Charles Rosher was a founding member of the Cinema Camera Club who also joined the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. The magically reproduced Rosher's physical appearance was not described. Like Frederick Leigh Gardner, he was a supporter of the cabal's 'Lady of the Masquerade Ball' and agreed with her utilitarian stance on sacrificing members for the sake of larger objectives.

As a magician of the Golden Dawn, Rosher was capable of using the group's signature magic style, though his particular specialization was not specified. He formed a trio with Gardner and the Lady of the Masquerade Ball herself.

Rosher assisted the Lady in summoning and directing the spiritual being Taphthartharath through a ritual involving multiple participants. By working in concert with the others and performing his assigned role flawlessly, Rosher helped to complete the complex ceremony.

The Lady of the Masquerade Ball was an influential member of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. Her magically recreated form was that of a beautiful woman wearing an elegant red party dress which emphasized her figure, along with a featureless full-face mask. She was infamous for her eccentric behavior and self-centered desire to be the center of attention, always seeking to carry out her actions in the most dramatic and extravagant ways possible, even waiting for audiences to be present before acting. 

Despite her vanity, the Lady was a powerful and accomplished magician. She helped to spread word of the Golden Dawn and raise its prominence. Within the cabal, the Lady gathered a select group of followers into a exclusive inner circle called The Sphere, which included Charles Rosher and Frederick Leigh Gardner. The Lady was willing to sacrifice her subordinates without hesitation to achieve her goals, viewing them as disposable pawns, but she did appreciate the rare occasions when they showed a little rebelliousness.

The Lady possessed the rare ability to summon and command Taphthartharath, a spiritual being said to come from the planet Mercury. Using a team of four magicians and a special nursery rhyme-like incantation, she could gather energy from a point representing Mercury and then drop it on a target area like an imperceptible bombing attack.

Israel Regardie was not a member of the original Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn but rather joined one of its splintered offshoots long after the main cabal had collapsed. Along with several other newcomers, Regardie hoped to restore the Golden Dawn to its former glory but their efforts ultimately proved futile.

Like his contemporary Netta Fornario, Regardie was magically reproduced and summoned back as part of an elaborate defensive measure against the return of Aleister Crowley. The false Regardie's physical appearance went undescribed but he wielded the same Golden-style magic as the rest of the group.

Regardies's preferred magical tools were a set of Enochian chess pieces shaped to resemble various Egyptian deities. By positioning these pieces in specific patterns, Regardie may have been able to mystically manipulate others, somewhat like how the Enochian chess 'angels' and 'demons' were said to represent the light and dark aspects of the human psyche.

Netta Fornario was a later recruit to the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, joining the cabal long after its original heyday had passed. She was one of several members who made a futile effort to revive the Golden Dawn and recapture its former prestige and power. The attempt was doomed to fail.

Later, Netta was among the Golden Dawn members who were magically recreated as a countermeasure against the reappearance of Aleister Crowley. This false version of Netta had the appearance of a woman with black braided hair adorned with a blackened silver accessory. Netta's simulacrum, like the other copies, could wield the cabal's signature magic.

The false Netta made use of an unnamed blackened silver tool, possibly a wand or ritual dagger, as well as a silver cross which had been stained to an ominous pitch black. She displayed the ability to cling to sheer surfaces with the ease of a lizard or amphibian, hinting at some body-enhancing spells.

Portugal is a country located in the far southwest of continental Europe, bordering Spain to the east and north. Its capital and largest city is Lisbon. The official language is Portuguese. 

Prior to the Blue Research incident, a Portuguese magic cabal operated a child trafficking market which was later destroyed. Portugal was also home to the Seventh Age Weapon Laboratory in Bragança, one of many facilities involved in the Gemstone Mining plot which imprisoned gemstones for research purposes. This lab was infiltrated by Misaka 17403, one of the Sisters deployed to liberate the captive gemstones.

Gemstone Mining refers to a series of incidents orchestrated by the CIA lasting from at least May to mid-October, in which 50 research organizations around the world targeted and imprisoned gemstones for study, in hopes of starting their own esper development programs. This plot was part of an American attempt to investigate the occult, codenamed Knowledge 12.

The CIA leaked a list of gemstone targets to these organizations and implanted spies to monitor their research. When Academy City discovered this scheme, they dispatched the Sisters in a simultaneous global operation to destroy the labs and rescue the captive gemstones before they could be harmed. Aleister Crowley allowed the operation to proceed.

The Blue Research is the world's largest marine survey ship, designed to search for oil deposits in the ocean. Its unique structure resembles three 500 meter tankers lined up side-by-side with a large segmented metal sheet on top covered in cranes. One end has a submarine-bearing winch while another section stores components for constructing offshore oil platforms.

This vessel was the main setting for a certain incident involving the magic cabal Dusk Exit, who attempted to use the ship to acquire funds for purchasing trafficked children. Their plot was ultimately foiled.

Spain is a country occupying most of the Iberian Peninsula in southwest Europe, with its capital in Madrid. It is a predominantly Roman Catholic nation but also a cultural crossroads, with Voodoo among its influences. There is lingering animosity between Spanish and English magic cabals, such as one called Armada which seeks to restore Spain's naval power.

Spain was involved in the international race to recover the remains of the destroyed supercomputer Tree Diagram. It is also home to various magic-related sites and groups, such as Barcelona which was struck by one of the golden arms that rose across the world as Fiamma's spell took effect. The country has its own space program as well.

France is a country in Western Europe bordered by Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Andorra, and Spain. Its capital and largest city is Paris. France has a population that is 80% Catholic.

Throughout history, France has had a rivalry with the United Kingdom, stemming from events such as the Norman conquest of England under William the Conqueror, the Hundred Years' War, and the Napoleonic Wars. Influential French women like Joan of Arc and Marie Antoinette have greatly shaped the nation's course. The mysterious Maiden of Versailles is said to secretly rule France as a powerful magician.

During the events surrounding World War III, France allied with the Roman Catholic Church against the UK. French forces attempted to invade by solidifying the English Channel and clashing with the Anglicans. The Maiden herself crossed swords with Carissa during the battle. France also suffered damage to its landmarks during the Star of Bethlehem's construction.

Brazil is the largest country in both South America and Latin America, and the fifth largest in the world by both area and population. Its capital is Brasilia while its most populous city is Sao Paulo. The official language is Portuguese.

Misaka Tabigake once visited the slums of Rio de Janeiro on business and met a young girl named Ines, who was on the brink of committing a murder-suicide due to poverty and debt. Tabigake convinced her there were other options and pointed her to the minute amounts of gold in discarded electronics all around her. Ines used this knowledge to start a successful recycling business and break the barrier between rich and poor.

Brazil was also one of the many countries involved in the CIA's Gemstone Mining plot. One of the facilities, the World Awakening Alliance in Codajas, was infiltrated by Misaka 17403 during the Sister's simultaneous global operation to rescue the imprisoned gemstones.

Ines is a young girl from the slums of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. She has light brown skin and a Latin face, of an age reminding Misaka Tabigake of his own daughter. Originally from an impoverished family, Ines was driven to the brink of murder-suicide due to overwhelming debt, seeing no hope of escaping poverty.

Her life changed after a chance encounter with Tabigake, who convinced her she had other options. Following his advice, Ines began gathering minute amounts of gold from discarded electronics to pay her debts. Her efforts gradually expanded into a successful recycling business that broke the barrier between rich and poor in Brazil.

Despite becoming wealthy, Ines still dresses the same as before. She has a pragmatic intelligence and strong determination to change the world for the better, even with limited education. Ines' success story attracted major media attention, with her being interviewed at a high-class hotel and commended by Brazil's Minister of the Environment.

Misaka Tabigake is the father of Misaka Mikoto, husband of Misaka Misuzu, and a world-traveling consultant and entrepreneur whose job is to find and fix the world's problems. He is a tall, bearded man in his late 30s with a well-featured face and an aura befitting of back alleys, inadvertently intimidating those he meets. In truth, Tabigake is intelligent, helpful and deeply loves his family.

Tabigake's travels have given him high-level global contacts, from a Brazilian official requesting him to handle their illegal dumping issue, to Aleister Crowley himself. He threatened Aleister over rumors of cloned girls resembling Mikoto. Quick-witted and analytical, Tabigake can discern a person's situation at a glance and figure out what a given location or industry lacks in order to give helpful advice.

Though not afraid to get his hands dirty, Tabigake prefers non-violent solutions and is said to always come up with at least three peaceful options to any problem. He has connections with groups like the RAF and has worked with Kamijou Touma's father Touya, a similarly globe-trotting businessman.

Archangel Raphael is an angel known as "The Medicine of God" who represents the element of earth. He is one of the only archangels mentioned by name in the Bible, specifically in the Book of Tobit. Along with Gabriel and Michael, Raphael is one of the three archangels recognized by the Catholic Church.

Raphael is said to protect adventurers and is associated with the planet Mercury. Terra of the Left, a member of God's Right Seat, is aligned with Raphael. 

During a battle between the reproduced Mathers and Aleister Crowley, Mathers summoned the four archangels representing the elements, including Raphael. However, Aleister quickly dispelled them by targeting Uriel with a banishing spell, which dragged the others down with him.

Cendrillon is a French magician formerly affiliated with the magic cabal Gremlin. She has blonde hair, white skin, and a slender, well-featured face. Her magical abilities are based on the fairy tale Cinderella. Cendrillon wears an elaborate princess-like dress made of many thin membrane layers.

After being turned into a table by Marian Slingeneyer and later restored by Ollerus, Cendrillon gained the ability to reconstruct her body if the proper ingredients are used. However, mistakes in the process can lead to her form being altered, such as when Mugino Shizuri accidentally reverted her to a 12-13 year old girl's body.

Cendrillon is a merciless fighter, using her speed-enhancing magic and the powers of her foes against them. She is fiercely loyal to her comrades, resisting interrogation under torture. However, any betrayal earns Cendrillon's scorn and vengeful wrath. She is highly intelligent and resourceful, able to improvise medical equipment from nearby objects.

Cinesic Evers is a French mercenary and the field commander of the Trident private military company forces during the invasion of Hawaii. He wears an old-fashioned French military officer's uniform, suggesting he was once a high-ranking member of the French navy before losing his position, possibly in the aftermath of British Halloween. 

Evers has great confidence in Trident's capabilities and is willing to sacrifice himself for their mission's success. He also cares about the well-being of his troops, surrendering in hopes of them receiving lighter sentences for cooperating.

As commander, Evers directed Trident's invasion forces from behind the scenes for most of the operation. Near the end, he concentrated their attack on the site of the battle between Saronia A. Irivika and Kamijou Touma, gambling the invasion's outcome on the result. After Touma's victory, Evers was forced to negotiate Trident's surrender to the United States.

Eiker Lugoni is a French terrorist who, along with his accomplice Musset, attempted to hijack the Sky Bus 365 as part of an anti-England plot. Their goal was to force the destruction of the United Kingdom's airline master recorders in retribution for the Eurotunnel bombing, which they blamed on the UK.

As the mastermind behind the hijacking plan, Eiker had Musset board the plane in Academy City to exploit a structural weakness and infiltrate the flight systems. Eiker himself later snuck into the cargo hold in Paris with explosives as a backup measure. 

A zealous French patriot, Eiker sees England as guilty without evidence. He is willing to sacrifice civilian lives and his own for his cause. When confronted by Kamijou Touma, Eiker engaged him in hand-to-hand combat but was eventually subdued. He made one final attempt to destroy the plane with a grenade but was stopped by the efforts of Touma and Stiyl Magnus before being arrested.

Harris Nicholagene is a twig of a young man who lives in Calais. He was researching mandrakes and environmental maintenance, with a preference for mandrakes with a feminine appearance to include an opposite nature and increase his inner masculinity. Harris objects to being called a pervert for this preference.

Within the month prior to a certain incident, Harris made use of a shared ceremonial ground, unknowingly becoming part of a larger summoning ceremony. He was later abducted and interrogated regarding the incident, answering truthfully about his own unrelated activities.

As a magician, Harris is capable of using summoning ceremonies to create mandrakes. His exact capabilities are unknown, but he had plans to grow the mandrakes in a sealed glass greenhouse and remake their environment to study the effects.

The Maiden of Versailles, also known as the Holy Woman of Versailles and Femme Fatale, is the true power behind the scenes in France. She is the twin sister of Elizalina and one of Europe's most powerful magicians. The Maiden has pale unhealthy looking skin, sunken eyes, and long pale blonde hair worn back with a headband. She wears an elegant white dress in contrast to her sickly appearance. 

The Maiden is said to be the latest in a line of women with a special disposition who have greatly shaped France's history, alongside figures like Joan of Arc and Marie Antoinette. Supposedly under house arrest and stripped of power by the French government, this was actually a ruse to fool her enemies.

Wielding the powerful Durandal sword, the Maiden allied France with the Roman Catholic Church in World War III and personally clashed with Second Princess Carissa of the United Kingdom in the Battle of Dover Strait, moving faster than the speed of sound. She later fought alongside Carissa against the archangel Misha Kreutzev, matching her superhuman speed and strength.

Musset is a French anti-England terrorist who attempted to hijack the Sky Bus 365 airliner alongside his partner Eiker Lugoni. Their goal was to force the United Kingdom to destroy their airline master recorders in retaliation for the Eurotunnel bombing, which they blamed on the UK without evidence. 

As the agent aboard the plane, Musset's role was to exploit a known structural defect and infiltrate the flight systems using a special cellphone. He boarded in Academy City under a false name and brought an animal bone knife to bypass metal detectors. Throughout the operation, Musset was nervous and fidgety as his plans quickly went awry.

After his electronic sabotage was foiled, Musset resorted to taking Index hostage. He was soon confronted and overpowered by Kamijou Touma in hand-to-hand combat. Musset made one last attempt to contact Eiker before Touma defeated him for good. He was later arrested after the plane landed safely.

Peter Wellgo is a tall pale blond man in his fifties with some grey in his hair. He wears a high-class custom suit and his muscles are starting to wither due to age. Wellgo is a member of a French Academy City cooperative institution.

Wellgo collaborated with the higher-ups of a Russian shopping mall linked to Academy City in a plan to detonate a Solntse hydrogen bomb inside the city itself. He made arrangements to ensure blame would not fall on his group should their Russian partners fail. 

After the plan's discovery, Wellgo attempted to continue it for his institution's benefit while framing a group called Project Code EIC. He tried to launch the bomb's core into space and set up explosions to cover his tracks. When confronted by Misaka Mikoto, Wellgo smiled and repeatedly denied responsibility, portraying himself as a mere cog in the machine. His final attempt to detonate a damaged rocket was thwarted by Mikoto's quick thinking. Heavily injured by a fall while fleeing, Wellgo was taken into custody alive thanks to Lessar.

Plum Mordosié is a female magician who made use of a shared ceremonial ground hidden in Calais's harbor district. At the time of her interrogation regarding a certain incident, she was wearing a bloody mourning dress and glaring with a sticky look in her eyes. 

Plum has a high opinion of herself and her magical abilities, considering a complex revenge murder plot she devised to be brilliant beyond others' understanding. She looks down on her intended victim as a "holier-than-thou asshole". During questioning, Plum became smug after letting her interrogator Agnese Sanctis think she lacked much of a plan, making it seem her revenge scheme was unlikely to succeed.

While Plum's exact capabilities are unknown, her murder plot involved using a summoning ceremony to disrupt her target's internal alchemical balance by extracting their physical body, believing this would cause them to destroy themselves with their own power. However, Plum was unknowingly made part of a larger summoning ritual and truthfully knew nothing about it when interrogated.

Rini Calculed is a young female magician around the same age as Agnese Sanctis. At the time of her interrogation, she was wearing pajamas and a see-through negligee. Rini made use of a shared ceremonial ground hidden in a container yard in Calais's harbor district.

Rini has an enthusiastic personality when it comes to her magical research on nightmares and astral projection. She is very particular about terminology, insisting on the word "nightmare" over "dream" much to her interrogator's annoyance. Rini also laughs at others' ignorance of her references and is defensive about her interest in wounds left on the body during astral experiences, denying that it is a bizarre form of self-harm or that she is "some kind of weirdo".

Rini's exact magical capabilities are unknown, but they relate to her research in weaponizing the mind's nocturnal journeys. She is interested in the physical marks left behind, such as scratches, seeing them as useful if properly controlled, giving the example of a placebo effect for inoperable tumors and aneurysms. Rini planned an experiment to find what injuries manifested after extracting her own soul or mind, believing that the tension of an unfamiliar environment could help her reach the desired state.

Rouen Nalberia is a large, muscular black man whose appearance suggests he could solve most of his daily problems with his fists rather than magic. He was one of several magicians making use of a shared ceremonial ground in a container yard in Calais's harbor district.

Rouen has a stubborn personality and is adamant about the potential of his magical research to enhance possibilities for all of humanity. He insists there must be a way to extract and utilize the results of his unique cooking process for extracting pure elements from food. When initially confronted by his captors, Rouen was defiant, confident and boastful of his prowess as a true magician. However, he quickly lost his composure and vomited after one of them vividly described the gruesome source of his bindings.

Rouen's exact capabilities are unknown, but his magical research focuses on developing a cooking method to extract and consume the compositional elements of food. He has succeeded in separating the elements within an enclosed space but has yet to find a way to bring them out without losing the product. Rouen planned to solve this issue using a summoning ceremony, but had not worked out all the complications at the time of his interrogation.

Archangel Uriel is a powerful angel known as "The Fire of God". He is one of the few angels mentioned in non-canonical religious texts, primarily appearing in rabbinical angelology. Uriel is said to stand at the gates of Eden with a fiery sword and was credited with warning Noah of the impending great flood.

Uriel's alignment is with the element of fire, though Fiamma of the Right suggests Uriel should be associated with earth instead, seeing the angel's current elemental affinity as a sign of the distortion in the natural laws of the world. Vento of the Front, a member of the Roman Catholic Church's God's Right Seat, is the human magician aligned with Uriel's power.

During a climactic battle, the magic god Mathers summoned Uriel and three other archangels representing the four elements. However, his foe Aleister Crowley quickly dispatched the angelic beings by targeting Uriel with a banishing spell, which had a chain effect that dragged the other three down with him. This strategic move effectively neutralized a key portion of Mathers' power in an instant.

The Anglican Church Women's Dormitory, also known as the Necessarius Women's Dormitory, is a residence located in Lambeth, London for female members of the Anglican Church and its 0th Parish, Necessarius. The building serves as bait for magicians hostile to the church, as attacking it would result in less civilian casualties compared to other targets. The dormitory has various defensive spells in place for protection.

Notable residents of the women's dormitory include Kanzaki Kaori, Sherry Cromwell, Orsola Aquinas, and the Agnese Forces. The dormitory was briefly featured when Kanzaki talked with Tsuchimikado Motoharu about recent events involving Touma Kamijou and the Amakusa-Style Remix of Church in the Adriatic Sea.

During the British Halloween, the dormitory was evacuated as the Knights of England took over London under martial law. Saiji of the Amakusa later braved the knights' guards and defensive spells to retrieve certain items he thought Kanzaki would need.

The Necessarius Underground Labyrinth refers to a complex network of tunnels beneath London used and maintained by the Church of Necessary Evil. Consisting of unused subway tunnels and stations, it stretches for kilometers with numerous real paths, fake routes, traps and detours to confuse and ensnare intruders. The labyrinth connects to the London Underground at certain points such as Lambeth Station.

The underground labyrinth was formerly used by Necessarius to test new recruits in a dangerous trial before they could become official members, with the Amakusa-Style Remix of Church being notable participants. However, due to the lethal nature of the test which resulted in many deaths, it was decommissioned for being too hazardous, though periodic exams may still be carried out.
