During the hunt for New Light, Itsuwa of the Amakusa confronted the fleeing Bayloupe and lured her into the labyrinth. Bayloupe soon fell victim to the traps within while trying to protect one of New Light's mystical artifacts.

Biagio Busoni is a ruthless and fanatical bishop of the Roman Catholic Church. He has the authority to command up to 1000 soldiers as part of his position. During the La Regina del Mare Adriatico affair, Biagio oversaw the project to weaponize the Queen of the Adriatic Sea for use against Academy City, willing to sacrifice the entire crew if needed to preserve the Church's reputation.

As a magician, Biagio utilizes several dozen cross necklaces which he can manipulate in various ways using the symbolism of different saints. Some of his magic includes expanding the size and thickness of crosses, multiplying their weight, and crushing targets under a great burden, drawing on tales of Saint Margaret, Saint Christopher and others.

Following his capture, Biagio was imprisoned in the Tower of London along with his accomplice Lidvia Lorenzetti. He remained defiant under interrogation by Stiyl Magnus and Agnese Sanctis until Lidvia offered to reveal what she knew in exchange for the release of her subordinates, much to Biagio's shock and anger.

St. George's Cathedral is the headquarters of the Anglican Church and its 0th Parish Necessarius, located in Lambeth, London just a short walk away from Lambeth Palace. Despite being the seat of Anglican power, its size is smaller compared to other major cathedrals like Westminster Abbey, St. Paul's Cathedral or Canterbury Cathedral.

While the exterior borrows architectural elements from Westminster Abbey's northern façade, the interior of St. George's is expansive with large stained glass windows. Necessarius makes use of the cathedral's vast underground complex which extends for kilometers beneath London, filled with real and false paths, traps and a spiritual item vault. These tunnels connect to landmarks like Lambeth Station.

Over its long history, St. George's Cathedral has been a place of terrible repute, housing Necessarius as they engaged in witch hunts, heresy trials and inquisitions to combat enemy magicians. It is suggested that even Joan of Arc resided there at one point. In modern times, it operates as the true power behind the Anglican Church while Canterbury is reduced to a mere figurehead position.

Canterbury Cathedral is the public headquarters of the Anglican Church, located in Canterbury, Kent, England. It is one of the oldest and most famous Christian structures in England. Known as the site of the archbishop's throne (cathedra), it serves as the Mother Church of the Anglican Communion and seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury.

The cathedral was originally founded in 597, rebuilt from 1070-1077, and largely rebuilt again in the Gothic style following a fire in 1174. It is one of the most visited sites in the United Kingdom, attracting over one million visitors annually.

While Canterbury Cathedral remains the official seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury, the actual governing power of the Church of England has shifted to St. George's Cathedral, with Canterbury becoming more of a figurehead. The cathedral is protected by magical defenses, including an anti-air system which fires pressurized red water based on the miracle of Thomas Becket's blood.

The Tower of London, officially Her Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic castle on the north bank of the River Thames in central London. It lies within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, separated from the eastern edge of the square mile of the City of London by the open space known as Tower Hill.

The White Tower, which gives the entire castle its name, was built by William the Conqueror in 1078 and was a resented symbol of oppression, inflicted upon London by the new ruling elite. The castle was used as a prison from 1100 until 1952, although that was not its primary purpose. A grand palace early in its history, it served as a royal residence.

In the modern day, the Tower of London serves as a museum and tourist attraction. However, it still secretly functions as a prison for magic side affairs, with the White Tower containing cells for magical prisoners. The tower houses numerous magical defenses and the core spiritual item sustaining the final barrier of the England-Londinium Fortress.

Egypt, officially the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a transcontinental country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and southwest corner of Asia by a land bridge formed by the Sinai Peninsula. It is the world's only contiguous Eurafrasian nation. Egypt is a Mediterranean country bordered by the Gaza Strip and Israel to the northeast, the Gulf of Aqaba to the east, the Red Sea to the east and south, Sudan to the south, and Libya to the west.

Egypt has one of the longest histories of any modern country, arising in the tenth millennium BC as one of the world's first nation states. Considered a cradle of civilization, Ancient Egypt experienced some of the earliest developments of writing, agriculture, urbanization, organized religion and central government. Iconic monuments such as the Giza Necropolis and its Great Sphinx, as well as the ruins of Memphis, Thebes, Karnak, and the Valley of the Kings, reflect this legacy and remain a significant focus of archaeological study and popular interest worldwide.

The history and mythology of ancient Egypt has long fascinated magicians and scholars. European magicians often visited Egypt seeking knowledge when they reach dead ends in their research. Aleister Crowley incorporated Egyptian gods like Isis, Osiris and Horus into his concept of Aeons after travelling there, and it was in Egypt that he contacted Aiwass and received the Book of the Law.

Germany, officially the Federal Republic of Germany, is a country in Central Europe. It is the second-most populous country in Europe after Russia, and the most populous member state of the European Union. Germany is situated between the Baltic and North seas to the north, and the Alps to the south; covering an area of 357,022 square kilometers, with a population of over 83 million within its 16 constituent states.

Various Germanic tribes have inhabited the northern parts of modern Germany since classical antiquity. A region named Germania was documented before AD 100. Beginning in the 10th century, German territories formed a central part of the Holy Roman Empire. During the 16th century, northern German regions became the center of the Protestant Reformation.

Germany has played a major role in the history of Western esotericism and magic. The legendary secret society of Rosicrucianism was said to have originated in Germany, and the Rosicrucian Order's main temple Lichte, Liebe, Leben is located there under the leadership of Anna Sprengel. Historically, Germany has been of interest to magicians seeking Norse and Germanic folklore and mythology as a basis for magical research and development.

The Necessarius Special Admission Test is an exam conducted by the Church of Necessary Evil for prospective members. Passing grants one official membership and a "Free Pass" allowing access to Necessarius facilities. The test is designed to assess an applicant's skill and mettle under pressure.

Historically, the exam involved navigating the trap-filled Necessarius Underground Labyrinth and mapping it within a time limit, with many dying in the process. Other extreme tests like being trapped in a submarine rigged to explode were also conducted. Due to the high fatality rate, the labyrinth exam was discontinued and a new test created.

The modern test takes place in a sealed white room, with the interior magically simulating a fictional crisis scenario the applicants must roleplay their way through, testing their ability to draw power from ley lines and telesma under stress. Though safer, it is still challenging enough that any error could prove fatal. Those who pass are awarded the Free Pass, an enchanted silver and red rosary that opens the way through Necessarius' magical barriers.

Leep, also known as the Priestess of Bastet, is an Egyptian magician with brown skin, long black hair and vertical slit pupils like a cat's. She wears a pink ankle-length camisole dress of thin material, a hooded black cloak decorated with ankhs along the hem and cat ears on the hood, a black fur belt with gold ornaments resembling a tail, and goes barefoot.

Leep greatly admired another magician called the Priestess of Sekhmet, seeing her as a strict older sister figure. However, that person refused to take Leep as an apprentice, so she had to learn by observation. After the Priestess of Sekhmet passed away, Leep sought to tell her story, but parts of her Book of the Dead containing her history had been stolen by grave robbers.

Using magic based on the cat goddess Bastet, Leep can command cats to steal information for her. By entering a trance and harming herself, she can also channel the power of Sekhmet, the violent lion goddess of slaughter, gaining bestial strength, speed and claws. Leep targeted Index to access her knowledge and reconstruct the Priestess of Sekhmet's Book of the Dead, but was ultimately defeated by Index, who conveyed a message from her idol telling Leep to become a freer magician.

Frau Halveria is a young female magician who specializes in Voodoo magic. In her studies, she attempted to perform the Ceremony of Ba Moun, a wicked spell that binds a contract with a wish-granting demon in exchange for annually sacrificing loved ones to it. However, Frau Halveria lost control of the demon and fell under its curse.

Desperate to temporarily escape the demon that would eventually devour her, Frau Halveria used a delivery app to have innocent couriers bring a package containing the demon to an abandoned building, where it would emerge and consume them. She repeated this process multiple times, leaving only a bicycle and pool of blood behind each incident.

When confronted by Angelene and the demon, Frau Halveria attempted to flee and used Voodoo magic to erect barriers against their pursuer, though they only delayed it. After a confession and change of heart due to Angelene's words, Frau Halveria resolved to sacrifice herself to ensure Angelene's survival, but both were saved when others dealt with the demon using fake corpses modeled after her.

Maid outfits are a recurring gag throughout the series, usually in the form of various uniforms worn by maids, women who provide domestic service. Tsuchimikado Motoharu is particularly fond of maid outfits, proclaiming his love for them second only to his sister. He often uses them to tease Kanzaki Kaori, resulting in her gaining an unwanted "legendary" reputation.

There have been many maid outfits mentioned or appearing in the series, ranging from the practical (Tsuchimikado Maika's professional uniform, Ryuuko Omiya's work clothes) to the outlandish ("Fallen Angel Maid", "Erotic Fallen Angel Maid", "Great Spirit Revealing Maid", "Super Rare Loli Ocean Demon King Bra Maid"). Some are worn by actual maids, while others are costumes obtained for or forced upon characters as a joke.

Maid outfits have been a source of humor, fanservice and occasionally plot relevance, such as when the Amakusa Christians discussed "fighting back" against Kanzaki's maid outfit with one for Itsuwa. They are iconic to Tsuchimikado Maika's character and the subject of an urban legend regarding a "cursed maid outfit" that influenced Saten Ruiko's choice of part-time job at a maid café.

The Priestess of Sekhmet was an Egyptian magician who specialized in magic based on the violent lioness goddess Sekhmet. She was seen as terribly cruel and merciless according to records, but in truth had a kind side to her. The Priestess had a weakness for sweet foods and would charge into battle to save a crying child even with nothing to gain. She never revealed anything about her past to anyone.

The Priestess's magic likely involved invoking Sekhmet's power by entering a trance state and shedding her own blood to become intoxicated with bloodlust, much like the goddess was said to do. This would grant her bestial claws, fangs, enhanced speed and strength. Her techniques were learned through observation by Leep, who greatly admired her.

After her death, grave robbers stole parts of the Priestess's Book of the Dead, which contained the truth of her life. Speaking through Index, who had reconstructed the grimoire, the Priestess expressed happiness that Leep had followed the path of Bastet rather than Sekhmet. She wished for Leep to become a magician who blessed others rather than shed blood as she had done. The Priestess revealed that while Leep had been her greatest trouble, she was also her greatest hope, having already moved far ahead of her as a magician.

The Curtana is the ceremonial sword used in the coronation of British monarchs. It represents the monarch's divine right to rule as the leader of the angels, with knights serving as their army. There are two known versions - the Curtana Original and the Curtana Second, created after the original was lost in the 17th century.

Both swords grant the wielder, if they are of royal blood, immense power based on that of Archangel Michael within the borders of the United Kingdom. The swords can also greatly empower the knights. The Curtana Original was unstable and risked overloading, requiring special facilities to keep it under control.

The Curtana Original and Second are both capable of using the All Dimensions Severing Spell, which cuts through higher and lower dimensions along the sword's swing, creating dimensional debris. The Original could also release its power in an explosion with a 500m radius. The Second was used by Queen Elizard, while the unstable Original was sought by Second Princess Carissa for her attempted coup.

Hrunting is a spiritual item sword wielded by the Knight Leader of the Knights of England. It is based on the sword of the same name from Norse and Anglo-Saxon legend, used by the hero Beowulf, though it also incorporates aspects of several other mythical weapons.

The sword is 80cm long with a 3cm wide silver blade covered in dark red. When the Knight Leader supplies it with Telesma in place of the blood of slain foes, Hrunting can grow to a gigantic 3.9m form with tremendous destructive power, durability and sharpness transcending ordinary physical laws. 

The Knight Leader can also use Hrunting with Pattern Magic, applying traits of different legendary weapons to his attacks, such as Gungnir's range, Fragarach's slicing power, or Brionac's speed. However, he can only use one pattern at a time.

Ascalon is a giant 3.5m long, 200kg sword given to Acqua of the Back by the Divination Operation Brigade. It is based on the holy sword St. George used to slay a dragon in legend and was designed as the ideal weapon to accomplish that feat. Acqua's coat of arms is inscribed on the side.

The sword has various angles, edges and attachments meant to cut through different parts of a dragon - thick blades for sinew, thin blades for fat, spikes for scales, wire for disemboweling, saws for bones, hooks for teeth and spikes for nerves. Magical power is directed to the appropriate section, signified by the blade changing color.

Ascalon also has a hidden 1m sword within its grip, connected to a wire which can extend and retract the blade or form a mace. Acqua made full use of Ascalon's abilities in his battles with the Knight Leader and Carissa during the British Halloween.

The Bunker Cluster is a cluster munition warhead developed independently by the United Kingdom. Considered a dreadful weapon, it was banned by a European treaty pushed by the Roman Catholic Church, though the UK secretly continued development. 

Typically delivered by cruise missiles flying near Mach 5, upon reaching the target, the Bunker Cluster releases around 200 special shells designed to pierce 50m underground. The shells' detonation depth can be timed, with a blast radius of 3km. 

Carissa threatened France with Bunker Clusters aimed at the Palace of Versailles in response to the Eurotunnel bombing. Later, she fired Bunker Clusters at her own forces during her coup attempt, to destroy Buckingham Palace along with the means of reproducing Curtana hidden inside. Though the damage was mitigated by Kanzaki Kaori's defense barrier, the palace and its surroundings still sustained heavy damage.

The Griffin Sky is a series of large unmanned mobile fortresses operated by the United Kingdom, resembling 80m wide hang gliders with a red color scheme and silver armor plating. Despite their size, they are inferior to the Coven Compass in flexibility and practicality.

While not as fast or high-flying as aircraft, the Griffin Sky excels in linked attacks. Their main weapons are 20m long red lances formed from their own shadows. However, this also makes them vulnerable, as stopping or twisting a lance will affect the fortress itself unless the connection is severed.

The Griffin Sky can operate in automatic mode, using minimal force, or manual mode, allowing the controller to specify a target like Windsor Castle and the level of destructive power used. Second Princess Carissa deployed around 20 Griffin Skies as part of her defensive line at Buckingham Palace during her attempted coup.

The Wimbledon is a destroyer warship operated by the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom. It is equipped with advanced radar and anti-air defenses accurate enough to target seagulls.

Most notably, the Wimbledon is armed with Bunker Cluster cruise missiles. It can ready at least 24 of these devastating warheads at a time. Combined with its precision, this makes the Wimbledon an immensely powerful weapon.

During the British Halloween, while patrolling the Strait of Dover, Carissa ordered the Wimbledon to fire Bunker Clusters at her own forces in Buckingham Palace after the Anglican Church began gaining the upper hand. The resulting destruction was only mitigated by Kanzaki Kaori's swift defensive preparations. Carissa also threatened to have the Wimbledon and four other destroyers unleash a total of 80 Bunker Clusters when the Knight Leader turned against her.

Divine Mother's Mercy is an ability possessed by Acqua of the Back, a former member of God's Right Seat. It allows the user to remove any negative side-effects of magic, including costs and limitations. This permits Acqua to use normal magic that even ordinary humans can cast, despite being a member of God's Right Seat. 

The ability also acts as a limiter removal on the human body itself, enabling superhuman speed and strength. It is described as the removal of any and all sin from the user, effectively making them a sinless human being. Divine Mother's Mercy can also grant immunity to punishment-based attacks by expiating the user's sins.

However, the ability has its weaknesses. Using it confirms one's status as a member of God's Right Seat, along with the associated vulnerabilities. It can be negated by Imagine Breaker. Removing physical limitations can also potentially harm the user's body when performing superhuman feats. Acqua temporarily lost this power after overusing it in a battle, but later regained it, only to lose it permanently after absorbing Telesma from the archangel Misha Kreutzev.

The Divination Operation Brigade, also known as the Astrological Surgery Brigade, is a nomadic magic cabal based in Russia. Its members come from all walks of life, with a diverse range of ages and genders. The group is known for its vast collection of spiritual items.  

As devout Christians, the Divination Operation Brigade follows the conflicts of others, using their magic to resolve situations and aid those in need. Their altruism eventually led to an overwhelming reliance on them, forcing the group to continuously travel across Russia to fulfill requests for assistance.

At some point, the Divination Operation Brigade became involved in a dispute with the Russian Orthodox Church, leading to a relentless pursuit by Church forces. The group was forced to flee in harsh subzero temperatures, their feet sinking into the snow. They were saved by the timely intervention of William Orwell near the border. The Divination Operation Brigade would later join forces with the Roman Catholic Church, expanding their influence. They provided Orwell with the spiritual item Ascalon as a replacement for his lost weapon.

Magic cabals are independent magical organizations, each following their own unique beliefs, rituals and practices. They tend to keep their secrets closely guarded and are usually careful about admitting new members. Betraying or defecting from a cabal is a grave offense that can lead to being hunted by the organization. There exists an unspoken agreement called the Job Counter, where if a cabal is formed to provide a certain service, another will appear to counteract them and prevent any single group from becoming too powerful.

Some magic cabals are actually Cabal Reserve Armies, which are more like clubs for those interested in magic rather than refined organizations. These usually have 3-5 members and engage in low-level activities like fortune telling or meditation, fading away without much impact. However, more serious groups can disguise themselves as these to hide their true capabilities.

The Golden Dawn was once the largest and most influential magic cabal in the UK and possibly the world. Its splintering resulted in many offshoots like the Dawn-Colored Sunlight. Cabals can be quite old and widespread, with the Rosicrucian Order considered the most famous from before the Golden Dawn era. Aztec cabals operate in Central America while the UK has the most overall.

Sleipnir is the name of a spiritual item used by the Russian Orthodox Church, based on the eight-legged horse of the same name from Norse mythology, which was the steed of the god Odin. The Sleipnir used by the church take the form of silver metal horses with eight legs.

These magical horses were designed to traverse snowy plains and function much like real horses in terms of riding and pulling carriages. They are a formidable asset to the Russian Orthodox Church's forces.

The church has used Sleipnir to pursue targets through the snow, such as chasing down the Divination Operation Brigade prior to the start of the story, and Sasha Kreutzev during the events surrounding the coup d'état of Second Princess Carissa.

Bayard is a metal horse, named after a magical bay horse from French folklore with the ability to change size. It is constructed of silver metal cast in the shape of a horse, measuring about 1 meter tall when folded up with its legs tucked under its body. The name "Bayard" is carved onto it.

Like a real horse, Bayard can carry a rider and move on auto-pilot to a pre-set destination. It has the special ability to evade and hide from magical detection. To use Bayard, one strokes its neck causing it to unfold and stand up. Tapping it signals the horse to start moving.

During the British Halloween, Acqua of the Back used Bayard to transport Princess Villian to a Necessarius hideout while he fought off the Knights of England who were attempting to execute her as part of Second Princess Carissa's coup.

Exit of the Evening Dusk, also known as Dusk Exit, is a British Golden-style magic cabal known for being extremely wasteful with their resources in pursuit of powerful magic. Their primary method involves sacrificing the lives of children as materials for spiritual items.

According to Leivinia Birdway, in order for the cabal to create a simple charm capable of conjuring a few biscuits, they would need to use up the lives of three children. The process of shattering the children's minds and turning them into empty shells for this purpose takes only around 0.7 seconds.

The cabal supported oil drilling operations in the Arctic Ocean in order to use the funds gained from it to purchase children from a Portuguese magic cabal acting as a "market". This indirectly led to the incident surrounding the Blue Research, as Dusk Exit's financial backing made the oil drilling ship a target.

Joan of Arc, also known as Jeanne d'Arc or St. Joan, was a French heroine who led a campaign to free France from the English during the latter part of the Hundred Years' War after receiving visions and hearing voices from God. She was born in the village of Domrémy in eastern France.

After successfully lifting the Siege of Orleans and leading the French to a series of victories, culminating in the coronation of Charles VII, Joan was eventually captured by the English. She was imprisoned, tried for heresy, and burnt at the stake in 1431 at the age of 19. A quarter-century later, a posthumous retrial declared her innocent and martyr. She was later canonized as a saint.

Joan was not born with any special abilities but began to develop them at the age of 13 after hearing a divine voice. While she led the French forces, a volunteer association attracted by her deeds formed to support her from the shadows. After her execution, this group became twisted by vengeance against the English and French, eventually becoming France's largest magic cabal, the Knights of Orléans.

The Knights of Orléans were the largest magic cabal in France prior to their destruction at the hands of William Orwell. They originated from a volunteer association of knights and commoners who supported Joan of Arc during her campaign against the English in the Hundred Years' War.

After Joan's execution in 1431, the group became twisted by a desire for vengeance against both the English who killed her and the French who failed to save her. Delving into the world of magic, they eventually became France's largest magic cabal. For centuries, the Knights of Orléans sought an individual possessing the same powers that Joan developed at age 13, an "Oracle of Arc", in order to enact their revenge.

They carried out experiments to try replicating Joan's powers in others. William Orwell eventually destroyed the cabal, saving a boy and girl who had been involved in the experiments, with the girl having been designated as the essence of the Oracle of Arc. Remnants of the cabal were theorized to have joined forces with the Maiden of Versailles during World War III.

Gods are higher beings, often with immense power and influence, that are usually the subject of worship in various religions. The concept and nature of gods can vary greatly between faiths.

In Christianity, God is seen as the one true absolute deity, defined by the Trinity as three persons in one - the Father, the Son (Jesus Christ) and the Holy Spirit. The unpronounceable tetragrammaton (YHVH) is used to represent God's name. In contrast, Norse mythology has a pantheon of gods like Odin who are powerful but not invincible, capable of being killed. Shinto has a broad concept of god (kami) encompassing various deities, spirits and phenomena.

Magic Gods, the highest level of magicians, are named after gods and have transcended normal magic to the point of being able to bend the world to their whim. However, their magic initially has an equal chance of success and failure until their possibilities unite. Some forms of magic are designed to combat gods, such as Ollerus's spell to reduce them to fairies/demons or Aleister's technique channeled through Noukan.

Considered the oldest living religion in the world, Hinduism encompasses a wide range of beliefs that are difficult to summarize due to the lack of a single unified doctrine. However, most Hindus believe in samsara (the cycle of birth, death and rebirth), moksha (liberation from that cycle) and regard the Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas and Itihasa as sacred texts.

Though Hinduism has a vast pantheon of deities, many modern practitioners see them as different forms or avatars of one supreme God, known variously as Brahman, Ishvara or other names, similar to the Christian Trinity. The major deities include the Trimurti of Brahma (The Creator), Vishnu (The Preserver) and Shiva (The Destroyer), and younger gods called Devas.

Hinduism and its mythology are used as a basis for magic, primarily by Indian magic cabals. Concepts, beings and items from Hinduism that have appeared include Astras, Ganesha, Garuda, Kali, mantras, Nataraja, Shakti, Shiva, Tejas and Vishnu. Figures from Hindu mythology were also invoked in spells used by magicians like Trismegistus and the reproduced Golden Dawn.

Laksha is an impatient Indian female sadhu, part of an unnamed Hindu sect. She dislikes fools, slowpokes and indecisive people. Laksha has a younger sister named Harisha, who was also part of the same sect.

Laksha pursues her sister to Academy City after Harisha abducts the sect's infant priestess Shakti to use in a ritual to save her own child. She attacks Touma and Index, believing they are aiding Harisha, using magic-powered chakrams. Laksha is surprised when Touma manages to break through her protective barrier.

After learning the truth behind the situation from Touma, Laksha accompanies him to where Harisha has taken Shakti and Index. She assists by holding off mantra-controlled animals while Touma stops the ritual. In the end, after Harisha's defeat, Laksha drags Touma along to see if his Imagine Breaker can cure her sister's child in India.

Harisha is an Indian magician formerly part of an unnamed Hindu sect along with her older sister Laksha. She was the nursing mother to the sect's infant priestess Shakti.

When Shakti fell ill due to a curse, the sect intended to use Harisha's child as a substitute. Though she initially went along with it, Harisha later regretted her choice. She abducted Shakti and fled to Academy City, needing to sacrifice the infant in a ritual and use Index's knowledge to save her own child.

Harisha's magic specializes in using mantras to control animals. She also uses them to construct a magic circle for a ritual to peer into Index's mind. During the ritual, Touma arrives to stop her. Though conflicted, Harisha eventually yields to his arguments. When the interrupted ritual causes the building to collapse, she stays behind to contain the power. Afterwards, Harisha and Laksha return to India with Touma, hoping his Imagine Breaker can cure Harisha's child.

In Hindu mythology, Astras were supernatural weapons wielded by the gods. However, the magic cabal Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens uses the term to refer to powers and weapons that utilize symbols associated with Hindu deities.

As humans cannot use the legendary Astras, the cabal has downsized versions that replicate the effects without the actual form. For example, a spear Astra could create stab wounds but not the spear itself. Astras cover various elements like fire, water, wind and earth.

Some known Astras include those related to the gods Agni, Shiva and Brahma. The Agni Astra forms the basis of Agni's Festival Fire. Shiva Astras like Trishula, Pashupata, Parashu, Pinaka and Nataraja have been used by Ureapaddy Exica. The Brahma Astra, the only "pure" Astra with a physical bow form, and Gandiva are her most powerful Astras, though she can only use the former incompletely due to the strain.

entries.content:
The Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens is an Indian magic cabal that uses Hindu mythology as the basis for their magic. They are known for pushing their members to the utmost limits of physical training through extreme traditional exercises and fasting, viewing the pain as a way to transcend human boundaries. This is in opposition to the calculated scientific methods used by Academy City. The cabal originally had around 50 members.

The cabal's magic revolves around the use of Astras, powers and weapons that are downsized imitations of those wielded by Hindu gods, reproducing the effects without the actual forms. In the past, they attempted the Astra Reorganization project to create a true Astra that could be used safely by a magician. It involved unifying the spirits of 15 members and redistributing them, but ultimately failed, killing all but one participant.

The sole survivor was Ureapaddy Exica, who became a patchwork existence housing the 15 spirits. She could incompletely wield the Brahma Astra, the project's only success, but at great personal risk. The cabal's unity was shattered by Ureapaddy's betrayal, leaving them in disarray.
entries.comment: Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens

entries.content:
Agni's Festival Fire is a destructive magic spell used by the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens magic cabal, derived from the Agni Astra. It is infamous for being used in an attack on a large sports gym in New Delhi two years before the start of the story.

The spell requires a large-scale setup involving magic circles painted with ultraviolet light on wind turbines to make them harder to detect. Each circle forms part of the greater spell, connected to a terminal which links to a single control point. By using the symbolism of the Hindu gods Shiva and Rudra, the center can send commands to the terminals. If the main control point is destroyed, the cabal can switch to a backup or convert a terminal into the new center.

When activated, even on a small scale, Agni's Festival Fire appears as a bluish-white lightning strike accompanied by the sound of fireworks, followed by an explosion of flames at the target site. The spell can be directed at specific targets by interfering with the turbine terminals to focus the power, though buildings in Academy City can disrupt the targeting due to wind flow. A chant is required to activate the spell.

India, officially the Republic of India, is a country in southern Asia and the seventh-largest in the world by area. It has the second-highest population after China. The capital is New Delhi while Mumbai is the largest city. Hindi and English are the official languages.

A number of magic cabals operate in India, often using Hindu mythology as a basis for their magic. The Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens is one such cabal, known to have attacked a gym in New Delhi with Agni's Festival Fire. Necessarius has a spiritual item in southern India for controlling nearby marine prisons. India benefits from its association with the UK, with 30% of British satellites launched from Indian sites, and is a popular choice for EU launches as well.

During World War III, India sided with Academy City against Russia. Some notable locations in India within the story include the St. Joseph Church, which had a pipe organ taken for the Star of Bethlehem, the Blueprint of the Gods research facility in Ahmednagar, and the Cape of Good Hope spiritual item.

The Aqua Tunnel is a submarine used as a cover for Necessarius's marine prisons. To the public, it appears as a luxurious glass submarine offering exclusive tours of the world's oceans, with tickets being extremely difficult for ordinary people to obtain.

In reality, there are twelve Aqua Tunnels, with eleven being the secret prisons and only one true luxury submarine to avoid suspicion. The submarines transport magical criminals captured by Necessarius around the seven seas on set routes. They were created to stop prisoners from escaping before reaching England.

The prison subs have no onboard control rooms to prevent hijacking attempts. Instead, they are remotely controlled by seven spiritual items called the Cape of Good Hope, one for each of the seas they operate in.

The Cape of Good Hope is the name given to a set of seven spiritual items used by Necessarius to remotely control their submarine prisons, the Aqua Tunnels, as they lack onboard control rooms to prevent hijacking. Each Cape covers a different one of the seven seas.

The Cape of Good Hope in India takes the form of a 70m wide floating grey cube, made of a material distinct from stone or steel. Panels and pipes like scaffolding connect the main building to the cube, extending and contracting as the cube rises and falls. Its size and range correspond to the sea it controls, with the Indian Ocean's having an effective range of over 9000km. The cube's altitude indicates the distance to the prison sub.

During the incident when prisoners used a Naglfar spell to take over an Aqua Tunnel and attempt to run it aground, Kanzaki Kaori visited the Cape of Good Hope in India during her investigation. After Kanzaki defeated the prisoners, control was returned to the item.

The Pataliputra Ruins are the remains of an ancient castle located in the city of Pataliputra, India. They are known to contain one or more grimoires that are sealed within and cannot be removed from the site.

Index Librorum Prohibitorum visited the Pataliputra Ruins at some point prior to the start of the story, along with several other prominent magical locations such as Mont Saint-Michel Abbey in France, the Vatican Library in Vatican City, Château de Compiègne in France and the Louvre Museum, also in France.

The Louvre Museum, officially the Musée du Louvre, is the world's most-visited museum, located in Paris, France. It is one of the city's major landmarks.

Index Librorum Prohibitorum visited the Louvre at some point prior to the start of the story, along with several other prominent magical locations like Mont Saint-Michel Abbey and the Vatican Library. The museum is known to have one or more grimoires magically sealed inside which cannot be removed from the premises.

Mont Saint-Michel Abbey is a highly recognizable landmark of France, located on a rocky tidal island of the same name. It is mentioned to have been visited by Index Librorum Prohibitorum before the start of the story, being one of several important magical places she went to, including the Vatican Library and the Louvre Museum. At least one grimoire is sealed within the abbey which cannot be taken out.

Mont Saint-Michel is known for its strong anti-magic defenses similar to St. George's Cathedral, which allowed some individuals inside to escape the effects of the Angel Fall spell. During World War III, the giant steeple of the abbey was torn off and flew to Russia, merging with many other church building parts to form the Star of Bethlehem.

The Vatican Library, officially known as the Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, is located in Vatican City. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world, holding a priceless collection of historical texts, including the Crowley-discovered Book of the Law which is now locked away. 

Index Librorum Prohibitorum visited the Vatican Library sometime before the start of the story, being one of several major magical sites she went to like Mont Saint-Michel Abbey and the Louvre Museum. The library's lower levels are known to have at least one grimoire magically sealed inside that cannot be removed.

During World War III, former Pope Matthai Reese gained access to the secret archives deep beneath the library, attempting to find a way to counter Fiamma of the Right's plans. Despite the mental strain, he persevered in analyzing the ancient spell books in order to open a path to a hope-filled future. He later coordinated with Vasilisa to incorporate Russian Orthodox spells after she freed their Patriarch.

The Château de Compiègne is a French royal residence constructed for King Louis XV and restored by Napoleon I. It is one of several prominent magical locations visited by Index Librorum Prohibitorum prior to the start of the story, along with places like the Vatican Library and Mont Saint-Michel Abbey.

Like the other major sites, the Château de Compiègne is known to have at least one grimoire magically sealed within it that cannot be removed from the premises.

Aurodasa Ginzhana was a magician and one of the higher-ranking members of the Hindu magic cabal known as the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens. As one of the cabal's decision-makers, Aurodasa held an important position and would be protected by lower-ranking members in case of an attack.

Aurodasa was killed by Ureapaddy Exica during the cabal's operation in Academy City, along with the rest of the leadership.

Kereelty Tanabrook was a magician and one of the higher-ranking members of the Hindu magic cabal known as the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens. As one of the cabal's decision-makers, Kereelty held an important position and would be protected by lower-ranking members in case of an attack.

Kereelty was killed by Ureapaddy Exica during the cabal's operation in Academy City, along with the rest of the leadership.

Sumtalak Shandeva was a magician and one of the higher-ranking members of the Hindu-based magic cabal known as the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens. As part of the cabal's decision-making body, Sumtalak held an important position that would warrant protection from subordinate members in the event of an attack.

However, Sumtalak was ultimately killed by Ureapaddy Exica when she turned against the other leaders during the cabal's operation in Academy City.

Kipsila Endinia was a male magician and high-ranking member of the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens, a Hindu magic cabal. As one of the cabal's decision-makers, he held an important position that granted him protection from lower members.

Kipsila conspired with the other leaders to attack Academy City under the pretense of opposing their body modification beliefs, while secretly planning to destroy the Endymion space elevator using Agni's Festival Fire. He helped establish a base in School District 7's Beehive after infiltrating the city.

When confronted by Ureapaddy Exica after her betrayal of the cabal, a gravely injured Kipsila realized that she had used him and the others as decoys for her own plan to use the Brahma Astra. Overwhelmed by fear and surrounded by her handiwork, Kipsila could only cower as Ureapaddy mocked him, stating his role was complete.

Pancavani Uddasala was a magician and one of the higher-ranking members of the Hindu magic cabal known as the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens. As one of the cabal's decision-makers, Pancavani held an important position and would be protected by lower-ranking members in case of an attack.

Pancavani was killed by Ureapaddy Exica during the cabal's operation in Academy City, along with the rest of the leadership.

Slasoma Anruda was a magician and one of the higher-ranking members of the Hindu magic cabal known as the Gate of the Gods Come from the Heavens. As one of the cabal's decision-makers, Slasoma held an important position and would be protected by lower-ranking members in case of an attack.

Slasoma was killed by Ureapaddy Exica during the cabal's operation in Academy City, along with the rest of the leadership.

Li Fanglan was the daughter of General Li and a member of the Li household. She had an untimely death when the necromancer Isaac Rosenthal murdered her entire family. 

After killing Li Fanglan and the others, Isaac used their corpses for his twisted experiments, reanimating them under his control. When authorities investigated the Li estate after the slaughter, Isaac proudly declared the undead family as his 'works of art', siccing them on the officials in response to comparisons to jiangshi.

The exact details of Li Fanglan's appearance, personality and abilities in life are unknown. As one of Isaac's creations, her reanimated corpse likely possessed unnatural strength, endurance and obedience to Isaac's commands, having lost any semblance of her original self.

Li, also known by his title of Ranger General, was a high-ranking military official and the father of Li Fanglan. As the patriarch of the Li household, he commanded significant respect.

General Li and his entire family met a grisly fate when the necromancer Isaac Rosenthal murdered them. After the slaughter, Isaac used the general's corpse, along with the rest of the family's remains, in his macabre experiments to create undead minions under his control.

When the authorities came to investigate the carnage at the Li estate, Isaac arrogantly presented his creations, including General Li's reanimated corpse, as his 'works of art'. Offended by their comparison to jiangshi, Isaac set his undead thralls to attack the officials. In undeath, the general's zombified body likely possessed enhanced strength and resilience, but none of his original self.

Kihara Nayuta is a young girl around 12-13 years old. She has blonde hair tied in two pigtails and often wears a red backpack. Due to the effects of drugs from experiments, her original hair and eye color have been altered.

Nayuta has a mischievous and competitive personality, though not to the cruel extent of many of her relatives. She is interested in Level 5 espers and aims to challenge and surpass them. Unlike most of her family, Nayuta is actually kind-hearted and empathetic, refusing to endanger children in experiments and insisting on informed consent from willing participants. This has made her somewhat of an outcast among the Kiharas.

Through drugs and surgeries, around 70% of Nayuta's body has been replaced with Academy City technology, rendering her a cyborg. This includes an artificial right eye capable of emitting a blinding flash. Her esper ability allows her to see AIM diffusion fields and overload the powers of other espers by manipulating their ability's flow and timing. With training, it is believed her power could allow her to defeat even Accelerator.

Haratani Yabumi is a young male esper who studies psychokinesis, though it is unknown if he has actually developed any abilities. He is described as being lower middle class.

Yabumi was attacked by Skill-Out members while in a shopping district and robbed of his possessions, including a new cell phone that served as a digital wallet. He was saved by the intervention of Sogiita Gunha. 

When Gunha explained his esper ability, Yabumi pointed out that what he described about applying a stimulus to a psychokinetic field shouldn't produce the effects demonstrated. He would later witness the battle between Gunha and Misaka Mikoto.

Yokosuka, also known as Yokosuka the Organ Crusher, is a huge muscular man and the leader of a Skill-Out gang near a shopping district in Academy City. As a Level 0, he is confident enough to take on even Level 5 espers.

When his subordinates were defeated by Sogiita Gunha after mugging Haratani Yabumi, Yokosuka confronted the esper himself. Despite taking an Amazing Punch from Gunha, Yokosuka was able to remain conscious and keep fighting, impressing the Level 5 with his tenacity. After his defeat, Yokosuka asked Gunha to finish him off with a better move than just Amazing Punch.

The encounter with Gunha left a strong impression on Yokosuka. Wanting to find a way to deal with him, he began working for another Level 5, Aihana Etsu. Yokosuka was roped into Aihana's schemes of using his name to solve other people's problems, getting paid 700 yen per hour despite his misgivings.

The Advanced Education Department is a now-abandoned facility located in School District 13 of Academy City. It was previously used to educate and care for Child Errors. The large complex includes an open space for the children to play, classrooms, showers, and a laboratory used for experiments.

Under the supervision of Kihara Gensei, teacher Kiyama Harumi was tasked with educating a group of Child Errors to prepare them for an upcoming experiment on controlling AIM diffusion fields. However, the experiment went horribly wrong, leaving the children comatose. Gensei forced the staff to cover up the incident and gather data rather than give the children immediate medical attention. It was later revealed this experiment was actually meant to analyze out-of-control espers and further his research into Crystallized Esper Essence.

After the incident, a disgusted Kiyama quit the facility and the comatose children were dispersed to various hospitals in the city. The Advanced Education Department was abandoned. Misaka Mikoto would later infiltrate the building looking for clues about the strange Poltergeist incidents plaguing the city, leading her to again cross paths with Kiyama.

Kihara Enshuu is a middle school-aged girl and member of the infamous Kihara family. She has black hair worn in buns on the sides of her head. Enshuu dresses in a pink sweater, miniskirt, asymmetrical boots and torn black stockings. She carries various devices hanging from her neck, including a cell phone, small TV and handheld device.

Despite being a Kihara, Enshuu lacks a certain "Kihara-ness" due to being isolated and imprisoned at a young age by rivals seeking to twist her development. As a result, she has a timid, naive and robotic demeanor. Enshuu constantly tries to prove herself as a proper Kihara. Though she lacks common knowledge, her mind naturally comprehends science, and she gravitates towards the purest, most evil applications of it.

Enshuu's esper ability allows her to perfectly mimic the thought patterns and skills of other people, primarily Kiharas, which she uses to compensate for her deficiencies. She wields an arsenal of scientific tools and weapons in pragmatic ways, such as using controlled mold as a biological weapon. Enshuu is considered the most dangerous Kihara in her debut arc despite her unorthodox background.

Produce was an unethical experiment conducted in Academy City that involved dissecting the brains of Child Errors in an attempt to locate the source of esper abilities, the part of the brain responsible for Personal Reality. The gruesome procedures treated the children like lab animals, chopping up their brains in a way compared to cutting a Christmas cake, in order to examine the sections and determine which parts correlated with their powers.

Produce was one of several research projects, along with initiatives like the Dark May Project, that unscrupulously used Child Errors as test subjects, exploiting the most vulnerable members of the City's population. The callous disregard for the damage inflicted on these children's minds and bodies was driven by a ruthless scientific curiosity to understand the fundamental nature of esper abilities at any cost.

Hishigata Mikihiko, a researcher involved with Produce, spent months systematically removing parts of the test subjects' bodies to determine where esper powers were concentrated. His findings that reducing the body's mass lowered esper output led him to theorize that reinforcing and enlarging the body could have the reverse effect and boost abilities, forming the basis for his later development of the Coffins as part of the Necromancer project.

Accelerator is a skinny teenager with pale skin, messy white hair and red eyes, a result of his ability blocking ultraviolet rays and reducing outside influences. He is often seen wearing black and white clothing, including a choker-style electrode that boosts his calculation abilities. After being shot, he relies on a crutch for mobility.

Initially cold-hearted and sadistic, Accelerator was shaped by Academy City's Dark Side and his early inability to have close relationships without harming others. He willingly joins the Level 6 Shift experiment to gain unmatched strength and a fearsome reputation. However, after being defeated by Kamijou Touma and meeting Last Order, Accelerator begins to change, determined to protect the remaining Sisters and later reflecting on his past cruelty.

Accelerator is ranked as Academy City's most powerful Level 5 esper. His namesake ability, or "One-Way Road", allows him to manipulate any vector, enabling him to drastically alter the trajectory and magnitude of motion and forces. By applying this to his own body, he can achieve superhuman speed, strength, and seeming invulnerability. He can even amplify and convert existing vectors around him, such as weight, to create an invisible force that he can use to great affect, such as forming a razor-thin blade that he can shoot at a target as a silent and invisible cutting attack or creating a force that absorbs everything in an area towards a designated point, as if mimicking a black hole's gravity. Accelerator's ability is automatic and extremely versatile, but suffers major setbacks after he is shot in the head, forcing him to rely on a choker-style electrode connected to the Misaka Network for his calculations. It is self-evident that the ability requires a great amount of calculating power from the esper, as it requires for Accelerator to take into account several vectors that he wants to redirect, and when activated, several variables are present when manipulating and controlling vectors. In fact, the combined brains of 10,000 level 3 Sisters are only able to make up less than half of Accelerator's calculating power.

Kuriba Ryouko is a middle school student with vertically striped light and dark hair, yellow eyes, and a darker section across the right side of her face from when she was split apart. She primarily wears a lab coat over a black and white school uniform, along with swirly glasses when working alone.

Kuriba is devoted to finding a way to save her ill mother, even volunteering to be split into two cyborgs as part of an experiment to gather the necessary data. She tends to accept sacrifice as a necessary condition to achieve something and doesn't highly value her own life. Despite her genius intellect, she can be reluctant to involve others in her problems.

A prodigy even before entering Academy City, Kuriba is a highly talented cyborg researcher knowledgeable enough to have devised many of the technologies used in her own cyborg body. These include safety limiters, artificial muscles, and suppressants to prevent flesh rejection. She was also behind the creation and distribution of the Indian Poker cards to help find a solution to the threat posed by her doppelganger.
